lens: POST-MORTEM: what went wrong, and what it cost (repo /home/user/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection, read-only; paths below are relative to it)
headline: The biggest losses were calendar time and compute, not modeling choices. 32 of the 58 days have no recorded work, about two-thirds of the free T4 quota went unused, and each lever that now carries the score (dense slice coverage, dread_soft labels, all-data training) was diagnosed 3 to 6 weeks before anyone acted on it. The project still runs about one big experiment per GPU-week under self-imposed limits (no cloud GPUs, no team merger, no API label read). The failure mode it named for itself is still active: gold-58 is gating a round-2 teacher after it overstated round 1 about 5×, and single LB reads are being spent on effects forecast below the LB's resolution. Separately, a trainer default (loss × (0.25+0.75|2y−1|)) mutes exactly the cells the teacher corrects. On this trajectory the honest landing is about 0.945. That is outside gold, which needs roughly top 20 of 4,999 (about 0.957 on today's board).

what_went_wrong.title: TIMELINE: when each real lever was found, and when it could have been
what_went_wrong.evidence: 08-06 FINDINGS.md:144-162 says 'the extractor is the solution', external data 'may be decisive', hand-label 250-400 reports. 08-10 §2e: the frozen-feature architecture 'cannot fine-tune'. 08-12 §2w: 'our own pipeline is 0.13 BELOW a thing we already have banked'. 08-13 §3p/D4: 'labels were never the ceiling'. 08-17 the host external-data post is drafted and never sent (REFERENCE.md:142-149). 08-18 §3z: 'the port sees 18 slices to pilkwang's 72'. 08-18 best LB 0.914. 08-19 is the last dated entry until 09-06. 09-06 board re-pulled ('moved +0.016 in 25 days', DECISIONS.md:25); 'efficiency track is the primary target' (DECISIONS.md:37-38); D2 = 18 slices at depth 0.5. 09-07 the 458 GB corpus is deleted on D3 and PLAN-C6 + PREMORTEM are written; Stage L is scheduled 09-07..09-15 and never runs (DATA.md:292-305). No dated entry 09-08..09-22. 09-23 Stage 0; the frontier's training script is read (it was cited at 0.924 by 09-06); D3 is amended; dread_soft is benched and dismissed as 'not scorable'. 09-24 Stage A +0.0149; goal = WIN; cloud-GPU question asked. 09-26 first own-model LB reads (Sub A 0.901, Sub B 0.936). 09-27 dread 0.916, which reverses D4; owner says 'no cloud GPUs'. 09-28 Sub B-dread 0.939; CNN teachers. 10-02/03 students 0.931 / 0.927; Ortho all-data finally running. Lags from diagnosis to action: dense coverage 37 days (08-18 to 09-24), labels-as-lever 45 days (08-13 to 09-27), frontier recipe 17+ days (by 09-06 to 09-23), NIfTI blame 35 days (about 08-19 to 09-23), all-data 10 days (09-23 to 10-03).
what_went_wrong.cost: Every lever now in the score arrived 3-6 weeks after the evidence for it existed.

what_went_wrong.title: 32 of 58 days dormant, and about two-thirds of the free GPU unused
what_went_wrong.evidence: A count of dates across every doc shows activity 08-07..08-19, a single burst on 09-06/07, then nothing until 09-23. Supporting points: no board pull from 08-12 to 09-06 (DECISIONS.md:25); 'The first GPU runs were pushed 2026-09-23' (archive RUNBOOK-2026-09-28:1270); no LB submission between 08-18 (0.914) and 09-26 (38 days). PIPELINE.md:189-198 budgeted ~25 of ~195 GPU-h ('Resource-rich, time-poor'). Usage I reconstructed: the week to 09-25 hit the 30.00 h cap (archive :1021); the week to 10-02 used about 30 h (c7 ~11, dread ~10.6, VLM ~2.5, R34 ×3 ~2, benches ~1); the week to 10-09 used about 26 h. That is ~90 T4-h used of ~270 available since early August.
what_went_wrong.cost: About 32 calendar days (55%) and ~135-180 T4-h of free quota. When the project was active it moved 0.914 → 0.939 in about 11 days. My estimate of the LB that never got built is 0.010-0.020.

what_went_wrong.title: 'Labels are not the binding constraint' (D4) was held for 45 days, and the cheapest lever was cancelled
what_went_wrong.evidence: D4 was measured 08-13, dropped, then RESTORED on 09-06 (DATA.md:39-60; DECISIONS.md:19). PIPELINE.md:128-144 says 'S3 labels: demoted, deliberately ... No API spend'. Stage L (a frontier-LLM severity read with the official criteria quoted verbatim, priced at $25-150 in DATA.md:257-275) was scheduled 09-07..09-15 and never ran: no targets_sev.csv exists, and labeling/model_labels.csv still holds 86 of the 303 planned hand labels. dread_soft was found on 09-23 and kept out because gold-58 cannot score it (DATA.md §11, row 'not scorable here'). Only the LB reversed D4, on 09-27 (0.901 → 0.916). The forum's 71st place reported +0.011 from label work at under $5 of API (archive RUNBOOK ~1300).
what_went_wrong.cost: The largest measured lever (+0.015 LB) arrived about 6 weeks late. Teacher→student started 09-28 instead of mid-August, which gave up roughly two label/teacher rounds.

what_went_wrong.title: D3: the NIfTI files were blamed for 0.085, and the 458 GB corpus was deleted on that false attribution
what_went_wrong.evidence: DECISIONS.md:17 (amended 09-23: the files cost nothing measurable; input sampling was the cause). AUDIT.md:368-390: contract_audit read two fields off a module train_port never imports and printed PASS. DECISIONS.md:124-125: 'The corpus was deleted on that attribution.' README.md:14.
what_went_wrong.cost: About 16 days with no local pixels. Today the Mac holds only the 32 GB Stage A cache. So every free Mac screen (the teachers, Z/R/N) runs a 224-336 px Stage A ResNet34 that sits 0.03-0.04 below the students it is supposed to inform, and anything at Stage B resolution needs Kaggle GPU.

what_went_wrong.title: The goal changed four times, and one plan budgeted 13% of the available GPU
what_went_wrong.evidence: The goal went from 'best model, not a placing' (PLAN-C6.md:3, 09-07) to 'efficiency track primary' (DECISIONS.md:37-38; PIPELINE.md:116, 09-06) to 'WIN' (09-24) to '0.965' (09-27). PIPELINE.md:21-29: 'the accuracy track is not reachable on the evidence, and the plan should stop pretending otherwise.' PREMORTEM.md §2 already priced the sequential C6 plan at 6-8 weeks against 45 days.
what_went_wrong.cost: About 18 days steered by a target later declared irrelevant. The September dormancy was effectively planned in.

what_went_wrong.title: The project kept rebuilding things it could have copied
what_went_wrong.evidence: In August, a frozen-DINOv2 feature cache with heads trained on the laptop ('the laptop only ever sees vectors', archive README-2026-08-17:747-750), after §2e had measured that it cannot fine-tune. §4b: 'trained a RadImageNet to 0.6924 while a 0.8514 one was a free download'. In September, train_windows ports the frontier's script with 'deliberate' differences (fusion/train_windows.py:25-38: a confidence weight, no gold epoch pick, windows that never straddle slots). Our Stage A dread Ortho reads 0.916 against the frontier's 0.928 on the same labels and geometry. That 0.012 'setup' gap was never broken down; the one factor named for it, 'gold ×3', turned out to have no source (RUNBOOK.md:198-207).
what_went_wrong.cost: About 3 weeks in August on an architecture that could not win. The unexplained 0.012 is inside every Ortho number.

what_went_wrong.title: Self-imposed resource limits: no cloud GPU, no merger, no radiologist, no host question, no API spend
what_went_wrong.evidence: Cloud GPUs (about 100 A100-h for $150-250) were asked about 09-24 (archive :1218) and declined 09-27 ('no cloud GPUs', archive :132). The team merger was declined (RUNBOOK.md:249). The host question was 'STILL UNASKED BY US, seven weeks' (REFERENCE.md:142). Kaggle TPU and Colab were skipped (archive :670). LOG.md:36: 'each week is one iteration'. Round 1's teacher was a ResNet34 because Ortho k-fold would cost '~32 GPU-h (a week's quota)' (archive :377).
what_went_wrong.cost: Roughly 10-20× less compute than a funded solo competitor. Inside this budget only one large experiment fits per GPU-week, which is why the round-1 teacher was the weakest model in the project.

what_went_wrong.title: Teacher round 1: a weak teacher, and a loss that mutes its corrections
what_went_wrong.evidence: The teacher was ResNet34 (0.8129 on the 691) teaching students at 0.853-0.93. On gold-58, report+ResNet reads 0.913 vs report+Ortho OOF 0.927 (DATA.md §12 item 2). labeling/build_student_targets.py:14-16: a conflict 'lands near 0.5'. fusion/train_windows.py:755-760 always multiplies the BCE by 0.25+0.75|2y−1|, so a 0.5 cell weighs 0.25 against 0.925 for an agreeing 0.05 or 0.95 cell (3.7× less). The weight was built for steven_v2, where 0.5 means 'not said' (train_windows.py:31), and was carried over silently to dread_soft (0.45 → weight 0.33; the Synovitis fill 0.35 → 0.48) and to the teacher targets. Result: gold-58 said +0.026; the CoAtNet student read −0.002 (noise), and the Ortho student's gain is about labels + input, with the teacher adding roughly 0 to +0.005 (RUNBOOK.md:63-64).
what_went_wrong.cost: About 17 GPU-h (CoAtNet 7.4 + Ortho ~9.5) and the 10-02 GPU week. The teacher route still has no LB proof.

what_went_wrong.title: Process overhead and fragile operations
what_went_wrong.evidence: There are 13,390 lines of markdown. The RUNBOOK reached 169 KB / 1,729 lines (LOG.md:11). 39 of the 50 commits since 09-28 touch docs only (3,875 lines of markdown churn vs 1,502 of code). There are 55+ owner-Q&A entries, many of them tangents (free-threaded Python 3.14t at LOG.md:114-126, speed/CUDA after winning, TDA, tensor decompositions, the Stanford work, fingerprint biometrics). Operations: the scheduled task stalled on a permission prompt on 09-25 (7 h) and again on 10-02; the Mac slept on 10-02/03, delaying reads by about 12 h; an app update killed a teacher fold on 09-28; a GPU-only log line killed the CoAtNet run on 10-02 (2.5 h). The CoAtNet student and dread ran on 1 of the 2 T4s (summary.json world=1, 3,800 s and 4,770 s per epoch).
what_went_wrong.cost: About 1 day per week of wall-clock on the critical path, about 9 T4-h on the single-GPU runs, and a large share of the owner's attention.

what_went_wrong.title: The leaderboard was barely used
what_went_wrong.evidence: About 13 submissions in 58 days (0.891, 0.899, 0.908, 0.914 in August; then A, B, c7, dread, B-dread, the (B) baseline, (B), the Ortho student and (A)). That is ~4.5% of the ~290 allowed, with a 38-day gap from 08-18 to 09-26. The first LB read of our own model came on 09-26, about day 51. Hidden-test reruns do not use quota (RUNBOOK.md:243-245).
what_went_wrong.cost: The only image-truth instrument larger than gold-58 (about 400 radiologist-read studies) sat idle, so label effects that neither the 691 nor gold-58 can judge waited weeks for an answer.

what_went_wrong.title: The failure mode the project named is still active, and it has a twin
what_went_wrong.evidence: DECISIONS.md:112-127 names it: 'A real measurement, aimed at a question it cannot answer.' Live instances on 10-03: (a) the plan gates round 2 on gold-58 vs 0.913, though gold-58 priced round 1 at +0.026 and the LB gave about 0 to +0.005, a ~5× overstatement; (b) (B) and the Ortho all-data read are single LB reads with the rule |Δ|<0.010 = noise, spent on effects forecast at 0 to +0.005, so 'noise' is the only possible answer; (c) a 224 px Stage A ResNet34 (roughly 0.88 LB-equivalent) screens levers meant for 0.93 models (Z, R, N); (d) gold-58 certifies the targets' AUROC while the trainer down-weights the cells that moved; (e) the '0.2× exchange rate' rests on two LB points that are each ±0.005. The twin: an underpowered or buggy null gets closed by a rule. Examples: §3t DINOv3 ('measured a NULL and wrote it down as a refutation', Aug); the VLM defect 'shelved per the rule' (09-26); the small CNN cut without trying the forum's recipe (09-27); N run with a weak teacher; zoom stopped at P 0.943.
what_went_wrong.cost: Systematic false negatives. The process guards against false positives, which are cheap at this rank, and lets go of the small, stackable gains a winner collects.

closed_too_early.title: Qwen3.5-2B VLM, shelved for a bug rather than a result
closed_too_early.why_reopen: The run did not test whether the VLM learns. The vision tower never trained, a defect the record calls 'cause not identified'. The forum's 54th place reports 0.950 from this exact model size. A different architecture family is the 'disagreeing model' the core's author says ensembles best. The code, builder and bench already exist.
closed_too_early.evidence: archive RUNBOOK-2026-09-28:930-946: predictions constant (per-label std ~0.0003); the 24 vision blocks did not move (median relative change 4.4e-4) while the merger moved 2.9%; 'the cheap next diagnostic is a ~15-min GPU run printing per-group gradient norms ... Not scheduled'. Forum report at archive :1301-1303.

closed_too_early.title: Small CNN as a main model and fast iteration engine
closed_too_early.why_reopen: It was cut after changing only lr, epochs and affine augmentation. The recipe that two top-100 teams report at 0.94+ (simple pooling, no attention head, 224-288 px) was never run. It costs about 2 min/epoch on a T4, against 36-80 min for Ortho, which makes it the only model that allows 10+ experiments a day under the current compute.
closed_too_early.evidence: archive :375: 'Never tried on a CNN: ... simple pooling instead of our attention head, more slices'. REFERENCE.md:316-319 (22nd and 85th place). fusion/runs_r34v2_B/summary.json: ~119 s/epoch. It is still only proposed as a side item (4) on 10-03.

closed_too_early.title: Cloud GPUs and the team merger
closed_too_early.why_reopen: These two owner closures cost more than any modeling decision. Training is allowed on any hardware; only inference must run on Kaggle. On 'I want that Kaggle master': Competitions Master is 1 gold + 2 silver medals, and team medals count. Only Grandmaster needs a solo gold. Gold here is roughly the top 20 (about 0.957 on today's board), which our trajectory does not reach.
closed_too_early.evidence: archive :1218 ($150-250 for ~100 A100-h), archive :132 ('no cloud GPUs'), RUNBOOK.md:249, LOG.md:36 ('each week is one iteration'). The merger deadline is 10-15.

closed_too_early.title: NYU Noisy Student (arm N)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: N used the weakest possible setup: ResNet34 teachers at 0.81 pseudo-labelling 7,140 knees for a ResNet34 student over 6 epochs, at P 0.75. That is an underpowered null, not a refutation. The obvious version was never tried: a strong teacher that never saw NYU (the public 0.928 CoAtNet plus our Ortho) and a strong student. The knees are already converted to Stage A.
closed_too_early.evidence: LOG.md:104-106 (+0.0035 ± 0.0051). REFERENCE.md:322-326: 22nd place says 'external data, even small amounts, can substantially increase score'. The frontier gained +0.010 going from 3,200 to 4,349 real knees.

closed_too_early.title: Zoom / crop views
closed_too_early.why_reopen: Zoom stopped on a P 0.943 near-miss, measured on the weak ResNet instrument. Its crop-specific gain landed on MCL (+0.052), one of the weakest findings. Every recent RSNA MRI/CT winner finds the structure, crops and classifies. This is worth one test on a strong model if compute appears.

closed_too_early.title: Using gold-58 the way the frontier does (epoch pick + top-3 weight average)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: The ban comes from a much larger selection: per-label picks among label tables on 29 studies. Picking 1 epoch of ~16 and averaging the top 3 is how the 0.928/0.933 core was made. Our recipe forbids it (train_windows.py:33-35), which may be part of the unexplained 0.012 setup gap. The cost is small, and the decision can be pre-registered for the finals.
closed_too_early.evidence: RUNBOOK.md:198-207 (the core's script: gold is the validation set; top-3 by gold AUC are averaged). DECISIONS.md:69 (the +0.0137 / −0.0034 figure comes from table-picking).

ideas.title: Rent GPUs for the last 19 days ($200-500)
ideas.mechanism: Every lever left is compute-bound: k-fold strong teachers, multi-round students, seeds, a second architecture family. One A100 or H100 does roughly 5-12× a T4 for this kind of bf16 training, so a full 5-fold Ortho or CoAtNet teacher round becomes about a day instead of a week of quota. Only inference has to run on Kaggle.
ideas.evidence_for: The archive itself priced ~100 A100-h at $150-250 (archive :1218), which is about 13-20 weeks of Kaggle quota. Round 1 used ResNet34 teachers only because Ortho k-fold cost a week (archive :377). Only ~64 Kaggle T4-h remain before 10-22.
ideas.evidence_against: The owner declined on 09-27. Setup takes 0.5-1 day (moving the Stage A/B caches or rebuilding from the competition download, environment parity with the Kaggle image). Competition data must stay on infrastructure only the team controls (rules §7).
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Enabler; it is the precondition for most of the +0.010-0.020 in the ideas below.
ideas.cost: $200-500 and about 1 engineering day
ideas.fastest_test: Today: rent one H100, run the Ortho-student-r1 build for 1 epoch, and compare s/epoch with Kaggle's 2,170 s on T4×2.

ideas.title: Drop the confidence weight for soft and teacher targets (plain BCE + pos_weight, as in the frontier)
ideas.mechanism: The trainer multiplies the loss by 0.25+0.75|2y−1|. A teacher-report conflict lands near 0.5 and gets weight 0.25, against 0.925 for an agreeing cell. The student therefore learns least from the cells the teacher fixed. dread_soft's graded levels (0.20/0.45) and the Synovitis fill are also down-weighted, which departs from the recipe that made the 0.928 core.
ideas.evidence_for: fusion/train_windows.py:755-760 applies it unconditionally, and the docstring (:31) justifies it only for steven_v2's 'not said' 0.5. labeling/build_student_targets.py:14-16 puts conflicts at ~0.5. Gold-58 said +0.026 for the targets; the student gained about 0 on the LB. The 0.012 'setup' gap to the frontier has never been decomposed.
ideas.evidence_against: Down-weighting uncertain cells is itself a legitimate confident-learning variant, so this may be neutral. Unmeasured.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.002 to +0.008 on a student (speculative)
ideas.cost: A one-line flag; a 7.4 GPU-h CoAtNet re-run, or about 1 h on a rented H100
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Same day on the Mac; 1 day on the LB
ideas.fastest_test: Mac: B′ ResNet34 on targets_round1_cnn with vs without the weight, scored on gold-58 (report only) and the 691. Then the CoAtNet student without the weight through the same --core-alone notebook, compared paired against 0.931/0.933.

ideas.title: A strong-teacher round: 5-fold Ortho Stage B (+ ImageNet-init CoAtNet) OOF on all 4,349 studies → report+ensemble targets → students
ideas.mechanism: Noisy student needs a teacher at least as good as the student. Round 1's teacher was 0.03-0.04 below every student. On gold-58 a report+Ortho-OOF target already reads 0.927 vs 0.913 for report+ResNet. The teachers need ImageNet or Ortho init, because the public CoAtNet has seen every training study.
ideas.evidence_for: DATA.md §12 item 2 (0.927). Forum: 71st place went 0.938 → 0.949 from teacher pseudo-labels; 36th place reports 0.950 and says 'labels were the bottleneck' (archive ~1300).
ideas.evidence_against: Gold→LB transfer was about 0.2× in round 1. It costs ~25-40 T4-h on Kaggle (all of next week), and the student read would land about 10-17 at the earliest. Gate it on the LB, not gold-58.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.005 to +0.015 single-model; about half that inside a blend
ideas.cost: About 5 H100-h (~$15-30) on cloud, or 25-40 Kaggle T4-h
ideas.time_to_first_signal: 2-3 days with cloud; about 10 days without
ideas.fastest_test: Reuse the Ortho r1 fold-0 model plus 4 more folds; build round-2 targets; train one all-data CoAtNet student without the weight; LB, paired vs 0.931.

ideas.title: Use 3-5 LB submissions a day as the image-truth instrument
ideas.mechanism: About 400 radiologist-read public studies are 7× gold-58, and they are the only instrument that can judge label and teacher changes. Hidden reruns use no quota, so a cheap model (the small CNN, or a short CoAtNet fine-tune) can be trained per label recipe and read daily. About 95 submissions remain; the project uses ~1 a day.
ideas.evidence_for: RUNBOOK.md:243-245 (hidden reruns off-quota). Label levers measure at +0.015, above the ±0.005 paired resolution. Gold-58 overstated round 1 about 5×.
ideas.evidence_against: Overfitting the public 30%. Only effects of 0.010 or more are readable per read. It needs a cheap model to scale.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Indirect: +0.005 to +0.010 through better decisions
ideas.cost: Submissions (free) plus cheap training runs
ideas.fastest_test: Small CNN, 5 folds, on dread_soft vs round-1 targets vs round-1 without the weight: 3 submissions in one day.

ideas.title: Run the forum's exact small-CNN recipe as the iteration engine and a 5-fold family
ideas.mechanism: ResNet34 or EffNet-B0 at 224-288 px with simple pooling, no attention MIL, and all slices. At about 2 min/epoch on a T4 it is 20-40× cheaper than Ortho. If it reaches 0.93-0.94 it becomes the teacher, the screening instrument and a diverse member.
ideas.evidence_for: REFERENCE.md:316-319 (two independent top-100 self-reports at 0.94+). archive :375 confirms it was never tried. fusion/runs_r34v2_B/summary.json shows ~119 s/epoch.
ideas.evidence_against: Self-reports, not code. Our attention-MIL ResNet34 fits training as well as Ortho but generalises 0.036 worse (archive ~350-360).
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.003 to +0.010 as a family; large gain in iteration speed
ideas.cost: About 1 Mac-night, or ~1 GPU-h for 5 folds
ideas.fastest_test: Mac: B′'s data with --pool avg (mean/max over all windows, no per-finding attention) at 288 px, 25 epochs; then read 5 folds on the LB.

ideas.title: Find and fix the VLM's frozen vision tower (a 15-min GPU diagnostic)
ideas.mechanism: Print per-group gradient norms each step under the exact GPU path (CUDA + autocast + DDP + checkpointing). Find why the vision blocks got no gradient, fix it, rerun the one-epoch check.
ideas.evidence_for: archive :930-946 says it is a defect, not slow learning. Forum 54th place: 0.950 at 384 px in about 3.5 h. It is a different family from the stack's members.
ideas.evidence_against: About 2.4 h/epoch on T4×2 and 3 epochs per session; its inference cost inside 9 h is untimed. The forum claim is the least-evidenced in the record.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.003 to +0.010 as a diverse family if it reaches ~0.94
ideas.cost: 0.25 GPU-h to diagnose; about 10 T4-h or ~1.5 H100-h for a full run
ideas.fastest_test: A 40-step GPU run logging the grad norm of qwen.visual.blocks.* vs the merger vs LoRA, and checking that the vision params receive gradient.

ideas.title: Team merger before 10-15
ideas.mechanism: Pools models, GPU quota (+30 h a week per member) and submissions. Rank-blending two disagreeing strong systems is the board's most reliable last-mile gain. Team medals count toward Competitions Master.
ideas.evidence_for: Three teams tie at 0.961, and the top 25 sit within about one LB SE. The 'disagreeing models ensemble better' self-report. LOG.md:39-40 already named the merger as 'the GPU lever'.
ideas.evidence_against: The owner declined (RUNBOOK.md:249). There is a submission-count constraint on merging. It needs a partner.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.005 to +0.015 (partner-dependent)
ideas.cost: Social/ego; zero GPU
ideas.fastest_test: Post in the team-up thread or message 2-3 teams in the 0.950-0.955 band this weekend.

ideas.title: Own the runtime: cut the 20 DINOv2 members, or build our own lean ensemble, and fit per-finding weights on 5-fold OOF
ideas.mechanism: The stack takes 8-9 of the 9 h, so stronger members cannot fit. The DINOv2 block is about 5% of the vote. A self-built ensemble (k folds × 2-3 families on cleaned labels) can be timed and weighted on 4,349-study OOF rather than on the public LB.
ideas.evidence_for: REFERENCE.md:343-347 (~5% of the vote). RUNBOOK.md:242-247 (Open item 4 has never been timed). The stack's weights look tuned on the public LB.
ideas.evidence_against: A blend change reads ±0.002, so this is hard to validate. Fitted weights were closed on gold (DECISIONS.md:67), though not on 4,349-study OOF.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.002 to +0.008 (mostly by making room for strong students)
ideas.cost: 1-2 engineering days, plus one timing run
ideas.fastest_test: Time each stack cell in one commit run over N test-like studies; build the cut stack; submit it paired against the full stack.

ideas.title: A frontier-LLM graded read (official criteria verbatim) as another weak-label source
ideas.mechanism: A different, stronger reader than steven/dread/Qwen-9B, used as one more teacher input rather than a replacement table. It covers severity-at-threshold and 'where'.
ideas.evidence_for: The host permits it (REFERENCE.md §1.1). DATA.md:257-275 priced it at $25-150. The forum's API label work cost under $5. A graded table (dread_soft) gave +0.015. The Qwen-9B rank-mean read +0.0054 even though it lost alone.
ideas.evidence_against: The text ceiling is about 0.90 on gold; LLM readers correlate at r≈0.82-0.995; OA severity is often missing from the text (DATA.md §12 item 8b).
ideas.cost: $20-150 and 1 day
ideas.fastest_test: A batch read of the 4,407 reports with structured outputs; rank-mean with dread_soft; one small-CNN LB read.

ideas.title: NYU Noisy Student with a strong teacher
ideas.mechanism: The public 0.928 CoAtNet plus Ortho (neither has seen NYU) pseudo-label the 7,140 converted NYU knees. A CoAtNet student trains on 4,349 real knees plus the NYU knees.
ideas.evidence_for: The frontier gained +0.010 from 1,149 extra real knees. The forum: 'external data even small amounts'. The data is already converted.
ideas.evidence_against: N was null with a weak teacher. NYU is 1.5 T, single-site, from 2018. It doubles training cost, and the agreement's terms apply to a derived copy on Kaggle.
ideas.cost: About 4 GPU-h to label, plus a ~2× student (cloud recommended)
ideas.fastest_test: Small-CNN arm N rerun with public-CoAtNet pseudo-labels instead of ResNet34's, on the 691.

ideas.title: Unconventional: transductive self-training on the hidden test inside the 9 h run
ideas.mechanism: Run the ensemble on the 1,322 test studies, fine-tune one fast member for one epoch on train plus test pseudo-labels inside the notebook, then re-predict. This adapts to the test's scanner and case mix.
ideas.evidence_for: It is legal in code competitions. Case mix differs strongly by scanner (FINDINGS.md §7.1, 0.14 spread in Medial OA prevalence), and harmonising it away hurt, which suggests a shift worth adapting to.
ideas.evidence_against: It needs 2-3 h of runtime the public stack does not have. It is risky, with no offline analogue except a simulated fold.
ideas.cost: 2-3 engineering days
ideas.fastest_test: Simulate offline: treat the 691 as 'test', pseudo-label it with the ensemble, fine-tune the ResNet for 1 epoch, compare against the unadapted model on the 691.

ideas.title: Unconventional: per-site / per-language report-bias correction
ideas.mechanism: Reports come from many readers with different thresholds; the test comes from one pair of radiologists. Estimate each site's (scanner fingerprint) and language's systematic report-vs-image offset from strong-teacher OOF disagreement, then shift that group's soft labels toward the image consensus.
ideas.evidence_for: 9 languages, 265 site fingerprints, and Turkish post-negation (REFERENCE.md §3). AUDIT 09-28 measured per-fold site shifts of 0.03-0.10 in pooled ranks. The graders' effusion→synovitis coupling (0.63/0.22) differs from the reports' (0.92/0.01).
ideas.evidence_against: Case mix is real (ComBat lost 0.013-0.032), so per-site offsets are confounded with prevalence. It needs strong teachers first.
ideas.cost: CPU only, about 1 day after the teachers exist
ideas.fastest_test: On round-1 OOF, check whether the report-minus-teacher rank gap per site or language is stable across folds before using it.

winner_would: Spend $200-500 on rented A100/H100 time for the last 19 days. The project's entire remaining Kaggle quota (~64 T4-h) is a few H100-days.
Run 20-60 trained models a week and use most of the 5 submissions a day, not ~1 a day. The project has used about 13 of ~290 so far.

Iterate on a cheap model (the forum's small CNN at ~2 min/epoch) with 5-fold OOF on all 4,349 studies plus seeds as the dev instrument (SE ~0.002), then port the winners to CoAtNet/Ortho. Do not judge everything on one 691 fold at SE ~0.004-0.005.

Treat labels as the main lever from week 1: several weak sources (dread_soft, steven, a $5-150 frontier-LLM graded read) feeding strong k-fold image teachers, then students over 2-3 rounds, with plain BCE on the soft targets.

Copy the frontier's training script exactly first (including its gold-58 epoch pick and top-3 average), confirm 0.928 alone, and only then change one thing at a time. Never carry an unexplained 0.012 'setup' gap.

Build its own ensemble sized to the 9 h limit (k folds × 2-3 families: CoAtNet, Ortho, a CNN, perhaps the VLM), timed per member, instead of squeezing members into a public stack that already takes 8-9 h.
Keep pre-registration and 2-SE rules for choosing the two finals. For daily development, take any effect that holds across 5-fold OOF and seeds, and confirm the stacked sum on the LB.
Treat a buggy or underpowered null as 'not tested', and fix the bug the same day (the VLM's 15-minute diagnostic).
Merge with a 0.950-0.955 team before 10-15 if solo cannot reach the top 20. Team gold counts toward Master.

Never let the machines sit idle: something always training, unattended steps that do not depend on a laptop lid, both T4s used on every run, and a 10-minute end-of-day log instead of a page-long RUNBOOK entry per result.

lens: How winners win: what past RSNA and medical-imaging Kaggle winners did, plus what this competition's public repos reveal, mapped onto this project. Network note: kaggle.com, huggingface.co and albumentations.ai are blocked by the egress proxy, so Kaggle writeups and the 18th-place HF blog were read only through search-engine snippets. GitHub READMEs were fetched directly. Tags: [DOC] = documented by the cited source; [INF] = my inference.
headline: Past RSNA winners, and this board's own top-100 posts, win in the ordinary Kaggle way. They train many cheap CNN members (folds × seeds × families), iterate a fast proxy hundreds of times, clean labels with strong out-of-fold ensembles, and judge on large instruments. This project spent its entire 30 T4-h/week on single-seed ViT-L runs (at most ~3 a week), has used ~13 of ~290 possible submissions, never bought compute, and trains on 12 randomly drawn windows out of 54–76. That draw leaves a lesion seen on 2–4 windows out of 35–71% of positive training bags. The highest-value move is to rent ~$200–500 of H100 time and turn every main model into a 5-fold / 3-seed ensemble that also serves as the round-2 teacher, fix the bag sampling, and spend the ~95 remaining free submissions as the image-graded instrument. Realistically that reaches 0.950–0.955 public. Winning at 0.961+ stays a long shot (<5%, my estimate); the gold zone (top 20, ~0.957) is perhaps 10–15%.

what_went_wrong.title: It took ~6 weeks to reach the recipe that was already public
what_went_wrong.evidence: DECISIONS.md D2: the model sampled 18 slices at depth 0.5 until it was fixed and measured on 09-24. CONFOUNDED-160: a 160 mm crop confound worth +0.0268 was hidden. D3 (amended 09-23): 'The corpus was deleted on that attribution', and it was the wrong attribution. MODEL.md §0: the frontier's training script was public but was only copied on 09-23. The rule extractor came 'last of six' (0.777). Before late September, LB results sat at 0.891–0.914.
what_went_wrong.cost: ~5–6 weeks of a ~10-week competition. Every lever after that (Stage B, dread_soft, teacher) was squeezed into the last 3 weeks.

what_went_wrong.title: The biggest backbone was paired with the smallest compute budget
what_went_wrong.evidence: RUNBOOK ▶ ORTHO ALL DATA: ViT-L Stage B takes 45 min/epoch on 2×T4, ~8.6 h per run. The GPU line is 30 h/week. One seed (42) per arm, and the seed floor was never measured (archive RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:1183, :1585). No rented or cloud GPU appears anywhere in the docs (grep: runpod / A100 / H100 / colab = none). Winners train on A100-class hardware: the lumbar 2nd-place README lists an A100 40GB and ~24 h; the mammography 1st place took ~8 days for 4 folds.
what_went_wrong.cost: 10–20× fewer experiments than a funded competitor. No fold or seed ensembles of the main models, and no recipe tuning. [INF] ~0.005–0.015 LB.

what_went_wrong.title: The leaderboard was treated as a rare event, even though it is the only large image-graded instrument
what_went_wrong.evidence: The docs record ~13 submission refs (grep for 5xxxxxxx ids). DECISIONS.md:87 still says 'A submission costs ~2 h... ~15/week', but RUNBOOK.md:244 established that only the ~6-minute commit run counts against quota. DATA.md:682 claims 'No instrument can confirm a one-finding fix'. That is wrong for a single-column swap: when 11 columns are identical, the macro delta is ΔAUC_k/12 and its noise comes only from that column (~±0.001 macro including 3-decimal rounding, i.e. ±0.012–0.015 on the finding over ~400 image-graded studies). The Vetri-78640/rsna-abnorm-det README reports that its comparison set of competitors made 16–287 submissions (median 117).
what_went_wrong.cost: ~60–80 image-graded reads will go unused by 10-22 at the current pace. Label decisions were pushed onto gold-58 (n=58), which cannot resolve them.

what_went_wrong.title: Label work was gated on an instrument that cannot see labels, and the gate passed something the LB then showed as null
what_went_wrong.evidence: The round-1 CNN teacher read +0.026 on gold-58 at P 0.994 (RUNBOOK Settled). On the LB, (B) student minus public = −0.002 (RUNBOOK.md:178), and the RUNBOOK forecast puts the teacher's own LB gain at ~0 to +0.005. An outside repo saw the same effect: SummerLinda/rsna-knee-weak-label-study removed 198 conflicting ACL labels, gaining +0.001–0.006 on report-label validation and losing −0.004 to −0.010 on expert-46.
what_went_wrong.cost: ~17 GPU-h (CoAtNet student 7.3 h plus a share of Ortho r1) and the 10-02 week went to a lever not yet proven on images.

what_went_wrong.title: The frontier's compute compromises were copied as if they were findings
what_went_wrong.evidence: fusion/train_windows.py:281 draws k=12 random windows from all slots (default --k 12, :526). Stage B has 82 windows (pipeline/slots96.py), ~76 in a typical study. By comb(N−w,12)/comb(N,12), a lesion visible on 2/3/4 windows is absent from 71/59/50% of positive training bags (Stage A, 54 windows: 60/46/35%). Augmentation is intensity ±10% only (train_windows.py:22, MODEL.md:30), epochs are 7–16, and there is one seed. None of these was A/B-tested on the main models. Every winner reviewed builds bags that contain the target region (lumbar crops around the predicted level, cervical per-vertebra crops, abdominal-trauma organ crops).
what_went_wrong.cost: Not measured. [INF] It plausibly explains part of the weakness on focal findings (MCL, menisci, fracture, contusion).

what_went_wrong.title: A rule against weak blend members grew into an aversion to ensembling
what_went_wrong.evidence: RUNBOOK rule 4 says 'Blend only strong members', and Settled says 'Cut: the blend of our own two models'. Yet the project's own data shows the 4-fold ResNet34 mean reading 0.832 on the 691 against 0.814 / 0.819 / 0.815 / 0.814 for single folds, +0.016 (archive RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:546). SIIM-ISIC 1st place: single-model LB-to-CV correlation ~0, 'the bigger the ensemble, the more stable the LB', 18 models. Abdominal-trauma 2023 1st place: 15 seeds × 4 folds.
what_went_wrong.cost: [INF] ~+0.005–0.010 LB per family left unclaimed, plus private-LB stability.

what_went_wrong.title: The project is locked inside the public stack's 8–9 h runtime
what_went_wrong.evidence: RUNBOOK Open item 4 and (C): Stage B Ortho inside the stack 'has never been timed', and the exchange rate means a member at 1/3 moves the stack only 0.2× its own gain. TranBaDat2607/RSNA-Knee-Abnormality-Detection shares one decode per study across all arms and both GPUs, and reaches 0.939 LB (gold 0.930) with the 4 public CoAtNets (v5 + v10 + v8 + gated) in ~2.5–3 h.
what_went_wrong.cost: No room for our own fold or seed members. The stack adds only +0.004 over that 3-hour lean set, at the price of ~6 extra hours.

closed_too_early.title: The small CNN as a main or ensemble family
closed_too_early.why_reopen: It was cut on a report-graded instrument and never put on the LB. Two top-100 competitors say a plain ResNet34/EffNet-B0 at 224–288 px with simple pooling scores 0.94+, and our 4-fold mean already closes most of the gap to Ortho on the 691. The 4 fold weights exist, so one submission settles where we stand.

Arm N used a ResNet34 teacher to train a ResNet34 student (with mostly the same data), the weakest possible form. With the 0.943 stack or a 5-fold ensemble as teacher, on rented GPUs, it is a different experiment.

With 4,999 teams, gold is the top 20 (~0.957 public today). A merger with a 0.950–0.955 team is the single largest step in gold probability available before 10-15.

closed_too_early.title: Zoom as an ensemble member (not as a lever)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: The rule correctly stopped zoom as a recipe change at P 0.943. For ensembling, though, a model that sees the joint line at 1.5× detail is diversity with a real crop-specific MCL signal. Winners keep near-miss variants as members when they disagree with the others.
closed_too_early.evidence: docs/LOG.md 09-29: Z − R +0.0070 ± 0.0045; MCL +0.052 crop-specific. REFERENCE §3.1b: 'Disagreeing models ensemble better' (Dread Development).

ideas.title: Rent GPU compute for training (inference stays on Kaggle)
ideas.mechanism: The rules limit only the submission notebook (9 h, 2×T4). Training can run anywhere: COMPETITION_RULES.txt has no training-compute clause, and winners must only document 'the required computational environment' (:110). An H100 at ~$2–3/h is roughly 6–10× a 2×T4 session for ViT-L/CoAtNet in bf16 [INF]. That turns the binding constraint from GPU-hours into engineering time and makes folds, seeds, families and higher resolution affordable.
ideas.evidence_for: Winners train on A100-class rigs (lumbar 2nd: A100 40GB, ~24 h; mammography 1st: ~8 days for 4 folds) [DOC, their READMEs]. Every item in the current plan is quota-bound (RUNBOOK GPU line: 30 h/week; Ortho all-data 8.6 h; 4 more Ortho folds = 20 GPU-h).
ideas.evidence_against: 0.5–1 day to set up. ~62 GB of Stage B shards must be pulled with `kaggle kernels output` (the DICOMs are deleted locally). The owner's budget is unknown. The MPS/CUDA paths differ, and a solo owner's attention is also a constraint.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: An enabler, not a gain by itself. Through ideas 4, 5, 9 and 11: +0.005–0.015 [INF].
ideas.cost: $150–500 total; 0.5–1 engineering day
ideas.fastest_test: Rent 1×H100 (RunPod / Lambda / Vast), pull one Stage B shard, and run train_windows --arch ortho --corpus stage_b on ~500 studies for 1 epoch with --compile. Compare s/step with the 2×T4 log (45 min/epoch on 4,349). If it is ≥5× faster, move all training there.

ideas.title: Submit the existing 4 ResNet34 teacher folds as one ensemble, alone (one submission, no training)
ideas.mechanism: This places our small-CNN recipe against the forum's 0.94+ on the image-graded LB. A read of ≥0.925 means a cheap, disagreeing family for the final ensemble. A read of ~0.90 means a ~0.04 recipe gap for the free Mac loop to hunt (pooling, bag size, epochs, augmentation).
ideas.evidence_for: Small CNNs at 0.94+ (REFERENCE.md:315). The 4-fold mean is 0.832 on the 691, against single folds at ~0.815 and Ortho dread at 0.844 (archive :546). The weights exist (archive :430).
ideas.evidence_against: Each fold trained on ~2,600 studies at 224 px with Stage A and attention MIL, which is not the forum recipe. Mapping the 691 to LB the way Ortho mapped (0.844→0.916, 0.853→0.927) predicts ~0.90.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Mainly diagnostic. As a final-B member, +0.002–0.005 if it reads ≥0.925 [INF].
ideas.cost: 1 submission, ~0 GPU-h (the hidden rerun is off-quota), 1–3 h to build if --ours-only loads a resnet34 last_meta
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Today, if built before the 17:00 PDT reset; otherwise tomorrow
ideas.fastest_test: build_submit_kernel.py --ours-only with the four fold last.pt files as arms and a rank-mean. Pre-register: report only; ≥0.925 lets the CNN family into final B, and ≤0.905 triggers the forum-recipe hunt on the Mac.

ideas.title: Stop hiding focal lesions in training: full-bag or per-slot-stratified MIL
ideas.mechanism: With k=12 random windows out of ~76 (Stage B) or 54 (Stage A), 35–71% of positive training bags for a lesion visible on 2–4 windows contain no lesion window. The attention head is told 'positive' while looking at none of the lesion, so it learns global proxies (effusion, edema) instead. Fix this by training on all windows (a small CNN can afford it), on per-slot stratified contiguous blocks, or by a short full-bag fine-tune of the head and top blocks on the big students.
ideas.evidence_for: Every RSNA winner reviewed builds bags that contain the target: lumbar 1st/2nd crops around the predicted level (2nd: 5–24 frames centred on it); cervical 1st, 15 slices per vertebra crop; abdominal-trauma 1st, organ crops [DOC]. SummerLinda: raising inference coverage from 24 windows to all (≤42) gave +0.0035 OOF with the CI above 0 [DOC]. [INF] Full bags may be why small CNNs do well for the forum posters.
ideas.evidence_against: The public 0.928 core trains this way and works. Across 16 epochs each positive still shows its lesion in ~30–65% of steps. Full bags cost ~4.5× per epoch. Diffuse findings (effusion, OA, synovitis) gain little.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.005–0.015 on the 691 for the CNN (focal findings); +0.003–0.008 LB once ported to a student [INF]
ideas.cost: ~5–8 Mac-h for two arms; 0 GPU-h
ideas.fastest_test: The Mac B′ recipe (ResNet34, 224, Stage A, dread_soft, seed 42; control B′ = 0.8129) against k=all (54) and against per-slot stratified k=15. Pre-register: HELPS iff paired Δ > 0 at P ≥ 0.95 on the 691 (a fixed-target comparison, which rule 3 allows). Report ACL / MCL / menisci / fracture / contusion as a subgroup.

ideas.title: Make each main model a 5-fold × 1–3-seed ensemble that also serves as the round-2 teacher
ideas.mechanism: The same runs give out-of-fold predictions on all 4,349 studies (round-2 targets: report + Ortho OOF) and an inference ensemble. Averaging folds and seeds removes single-run variance, which is what makes LB rankings stable.
ideas.evidence_for: Abdominal-trauma 1st: 15 seeds × 4 folds. SIIM-ISIC 1st: 18 models, 'the bigger the ensemble, the more stable the LB'. Mammography 1st: 4-fold ConvNeXt-S [DOC]. Our ResNet34: +0.016 on the 691 from 4 folds (archive :546). Gold diagnostic: report + Ortho OOF 0.927 vs report + ResNet34 0.913 (RUNBOOK plan context; DATA §12 item 2).
ideas.evidence_against: Inference time: Stage B Ortho per member is untimed and 5 members could take 5–7 h. Round 1's gold gain did not transfer to the LB. Each fold sees only 80% of the data, so finals should use all-data seeds.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.004–0.010 from ensembling; +0.000–0.008 from round-2 labels [INF]
ideas.cost: ~10–15 H100-h (~$30–50) versus ~45–60 T4-h (two weeks of quota) on Kaggle
ideas.fastest_test: First measure the seed floor and the ensemble gain in one step: a second seed of the Ortho r1 recipe (3,502 / 691), reporting seed1, seed2 and their rank-mean on the 691 (r1 = 0.8534).

ideas.title: A one-decode lean inference notebook as the robust final (final B)
ideas.mechanism: Decode each study once and stream it to every member on both T4s. Equal-rank families, nothing fitted on the public LB: the 4 public CoAtNets (0.939 in ~2.5–3 h, per TranBaDat) + Ortho-all + the CoAtNet student + seed or fold members + CNN folds. This uses the ~6 h the stack spends on low-weight members.
ideas.evidence_for: TranBaDat2607: one decode shared across arms and GPUs, 0.939 LB in 2.5–3 h [DOC]. The stack's weights look LB-tuned (REFERENCE §3.2, 'Where it could be improved' (1)), so its private score is probably below 0.943 [INF]. SIIM-ISIC: broad ensembles survive shake-ups.
ideas.evidence_against: 1–2 engineering days in build_submit_kernel. The lean base starts ~0.004 below the stack. Members must be timed.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Final B at ~0.945–0.950 public, and probably better than the stack-based final on private [INF]
ideas.cost: 1–2 engineering days; ~0.5 GPU-h of commit runs
ideas.fastest_test: Build the lean notebook with only the 4 public CoAtNets, confirm ~0.939 and log wall time per member, then add Ortho-all.

ideas.title: A leaderboard label lab: one fixed cheap model per label table, submitted alone and paired
ideas.mechanism: Label effects are large (+0.015 for dread_soft over steven_v2) and only the LB can see them. Train the same Mac ResNet34 (all data, same seed) on table X and on dread_soft, and submit both alone. The prediction correlation is high, so the paired noise is ~±0.003–0.005. Use this to judge round-1 vs round-2 targets, an LLM table, the Synovitis fix and gold-in-training before spending big-model GPU time.
ideas.evidence_for: DATA §11: dread_soft's win was visible only on the LB. Round-1's +0.026 on gold became ~0 on the LB. SummerLinda: a gain on report-label validation reversed on expert labels [DOC].
ideas.evidence_against: A label ranking found on ResNet34 may not transfer to ViT-L or CoAtNet. Each comparison costs 2 submissions. Some differences will be smaller than the noise.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Indirect: it selects the label changes worth +0.005–0.015 for the students [INF]
ideas.cost: 1–2 Mac-h + 1 submission per table
ideas.fastest_test: ResNet34 all-data on dread_soft vs on targets_round1_cnn (75757be8), same seed. Pre-register |Δ| < 0.006 = noise. This also checks whether the teacher's LB null was specific to the CoAtNet.

ideas.title: Single-column-swap probes for the four weak findings
ideas.mechanism: Change one finding's column inside the submission notebook and keep the other 11 identical. The LB delta is ΔAUC_k/12 with noise only from that column, so a +0.03 finding-level change is ~2σ on ~400 image-graded studies. Example probes: Synovitis := an Effusion-weighted variant; Lateral OA / PF OA taken from a different family.
ideas.evidence_for: Arithmetic (see closed_too_early). RUNBOOK: +0.05 on the four weak findings = +0.017 macro, more than any measured lever.
ideas.evidence_against: Picking among many probes overfits the public 30%. Rounding to 3 decimals limits resolution. It costs submissions.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.002–0.005 if one or two pre-registered fixes pass [INF]
ideas.cost: 1 submission per probe; 0 GPU-h
ideas.fastest_test: Sub B-dread's notebook with Synovitis replaced by rank-mean(Synovitis, Effusion), one pre-registered rule, one submission.

ideas.title: A criteria-aware graded label read from frontier LLMs (2–3 vendors)
ideas.mechanism: Prompt with the official severity criteria (REFERENCE §2), output dread_soft-style levels with the step at the graders' threshold, then rank-mean across vendors to break the correlated errors of a single reader.
ideas.evidence_for: The host permits hosted LLMs (REFERENCE §1.1). REFERENCE §5 item 2 was never run with a frontier model. Qwen-9B read Fracture +0.108 better than steven_v2 even while failing overall (DATA §11).
ideas.evidence_against: Public GPT reads are near-duplicates (|r| 0.87–0.95). The text ceiling is ~0.90 on gold (DATA §12). dread_soft cannot be scored on gold.
ideas.cost: $50–200 API + 1 engineering day; judged by the label lab
ideas.fastest_test: A single read of the 58 gold reports per vendor (<$5) vs steven_v2's 0.887, report only and done once. If ≥ steven_v2, label all 4,349 and send the table through the label lab.

ideas.title: A second-stage sequence head on out-of-fold window features (ICH-winner style)
ideas.mechanism: Dump per-window features from the fold models, then train a bi-GRU or 2-layer transformer per slot followed by per-finding attention, on full bags, in minutes on the Mac. It adds cross-slice context and trains the head without bag subsampling.
ideas.evidence_for: ICH 2019 1st: 'the key module of the pipeline is a sequence model'. Cervical 2022 1st: CNN → LSTM over 15 slices. Abdominal-trauma 2023 1st: CNN + GRU. Lumbar 2024 2nd: encoder → LSTM → attention [DOC]. PLAN.md §3.3 planned a slice transformer, but the current WindowMIL has none (train_windows.py:339–404).
ideas.evidence_against: It needs fold models (idea 4) to be clean. For all-data models the features are in-sample. It adds one more stage to inference.
ideas.cost: ~1–2 GPU-h per fold model to dump features; Mac minutes to train; ~1 engineering day
ideas.fastest_test: Using the 4 ResNet34 teacher folds: dump OOF window features on the Mac, train a GRU head on the 3,502, compare on the 691 against the folds' own OOF mean (0.832).

ideas.title: Noisy Student on the 7,140 cached NYU knees with a strong teacher
ideas.mechanism: The teacher is the 0.943 stack or our 5-fold ensemble, run on rented GPUs. The student trains on competition knees plus soft pseudo-labels from the NYU knees, with augmentation and dropout.
ideas.evidence_for: RANZCR 1st: 28k external pseudo-labelled images [DOC]. Lumbar 2nd: 0.5 × label loss + 0.5 × pseudo-label loss [DOC]. Forum: 'external data, even small amounts, can substantially increase score' (REFERENCE.md:323).

ideas.fastest_test: Rerun N with the teacher swapped from ResNet34 folds to Ortho r1 plus the CoAtNet student (both stronger), judged on the 691 against B′ as pre-registered before.

ideas.title: A high-resolution CNN family (ConvNeXt-S / EfficientNetV2-S at 448–512 px, near native 437 px)
ideas.mechanism: Thin structures (MCL, cartilage, meniscus) lose detail at 384. CNNs scale to resolution more cheaply than ViT-L, and a third architecture family adds disagreement to the ensemble.
ideas.evidence_for: Lumbar 1st: 512 px crops, ConvNeXt-small, 'convolution models were better than vits' (REFERENCE §4.5) [DOC]. Our R − B′ (resolution alone) +0.0089, P 0.979; Stage B +0.014 LB.
ideas.evidence_against: It needs a new cache (8 CPU kernels, ~1 h, as for Stage B) and more inference time.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.003–0.008 as a family [INF]
ideas.cost: ~1 h of Kaggle CPU kernels + ~5–10 H100-h
ideas.fastest_test: ConvNeXt-S at 448 on 3,502 / 691 against Ortho r1's 0.8534 at fixed targets.

winner_would: Fold and seed ensembles of every strong recipe. [DOC] Abdominal-trauma 2023 1st: 4-fold GroupKFold × 15 seeds. SIIM-ISIC 1st: 18 models, single-model LB-to-CV correlation ~0, bigger ensembles more stable. Mammography 1st: 4-fold ConvNeXt-S. [PROJECT] One seed per arm; seed floor never measured; own ResNet34 4-fold +0.016 on the 691 unused at inference. [GAP] ~0.005–0.010 LB.

A fast proxy loop and hundreds of experiments. [DOC] Tucker Arrants' method (REFERENCE §3.1b): report-label validation with a ~0.003 noise threshold, seeds, one change at a time. Vetri-78640 README: its comparison set of competitors used 16–287 submissions (median 117). [PROJECT] Main runs take 5–10 GPU-h and ~2–3 a week; ~13 submissions recorded. [GAP] The main recipe was never tuned. [INF] ~0.005–0.015.

Pay for training compute. [DOC] Lumbar 2nd trained on an A100 40GB (~24 h); mammography 1st spent ~8 days on 4 folds. [PROJECT] 30 T4-h/week plus a Mac; no rental considered. [GAP] 10–20× fewer GPU-hours; the root cause of the two habits above.

Prefer CNNs at high resolution for fine structures. [DOC] Lumbar 1st: 'convolution models were better than vits', ConvNeXt-small, 512 px crops. Forum: ResNet34 / EffNet-B0 at 0.94+. [PROJECT] Main bet on ViT-L Ortho; CNN used only as a teacher. [GAP] Compute misallocation more than an AUC gap. [INF] A 448–512 CNN family is +0.003–0.008.

Put the target region inside every training bag (localise, then crop or sample around it). [DOC] Lumbar 1st/2nd, cervical 1st, abdominal-trauma 1st, aneurysm 2025 1st (vessel-ROI masking). [PROJECT] 140 mm field and k=12 random windows; 50–71% of positive bags miss a 2–4-window lesion (Stage B). [GAP] Unmeasured; test it overnight on the Mac.

A sequence model over slices. [DOC] ICH 2019 1st ('key module'), cervical 1st LSTM, abdominal-trauma 1st GRU, lumbar 2nd LSTM → attention. [PROJECT] Per-finding attention MIL with slot/depth embeddings, no cross-window context. [GAP] [INF] +0.003–0.008.

Heavy augmentation, matched to longer training. [DOC] Abdominal-trauma 1st: flips, rotate ±25°, perspective. Lumbar 2nd: 'heavy augmentation, sequence reversal, left/right side mixing, manifold mixup', 9-rotation TTA. Lumbar 1st: coordinate jitter 'crucial'. [PROJECT] Intensity ±10% only on the main models; affine tried once on ResNet34 (arm C). [GAP] Unknown, [INF] 0–0.005. Note: medial/lateral flips are only safe with label swapping, and knee compartments are not symmetric.

Clean labels with strong out-of-fold ensembles and mix in pseudo-label loss. [DOC] Lumbar 2nd: confident learning on an OOF ensemble plus 0.5 × pseudo-label loss. RANZCR 1st: external pseudo-labels. HMS: a second stage on high-agreement labels. Board posts: '0.950 single models credit labels'. [PROJECT] One round with the weakest available teacher (ResNet34 recipe C, 0.806 on the 691); LB ~0. [GAP] Up to +0.01–0.02 with a strong teacher [INF], judged on the LB rather than gold.

External data, even a little. [DOC] Mammography 1st: 5 external datasets, about +0.02 F1 on OOF and private LB. Forum 22nd: 'even small amounts... substantially'. [PROJECT] fastMRI+ teacher cut (P 0.21); NYU pseudo-knees null with a weak teacher; OAI closed on its terms. [GAP] Unknown. [INF] Possibly part of what the top teams do that nobody posts.

Inference engineering to fit more members. [DOC] Mammography 1st: TensorRT. TranBaDat: one shared decode, 4 CoAtNets in 2.5–3 h → 0.939. [PROJECT] Bound to the 8–9 h public stack; (C) blocked on runtime. [GAP] Room for 4–8 members.

Pick finals by CV or robustness, with two different objectives. [DOC] SIIM-ISIC 1st: two ensembles, one per CV definition; survived a large shake-up. [PROJECT] Two pre-registered finals (A = stack + students, B = own blend), which matches. But A rides LB-tuned stack weights, so B is the real shake-up hedge and deserves the lean multi-member build.

Use every free submission on pre-registered, low-degree-of-freedom questions (which label table, which family, single-finding fixes), never on weight tuning. [INF from the median-117 statistic plus this competition's structure: the public LB, ~400 image-graded studies, is 7× gold-58.] [PROJECT] ~1–3 a day, often unused. [GAP] ~60–80 image-graded reads.
Team up for the last 0.005. [DOC] Top RSNA finishes are mostly teams (lumbar 2nd: 4; SIIM-ISIC 1st: 3). [PROJECT] Solo by choice, and Master does not require a solo gold.

A 19-day schedule [INF]. Day 0–1: rent GPUs; submit the ResNet34 4-fold alone; start the bag-sampling A/B on the Mac. Day 2–5: 5-fold Ortho + 5-fold CoAtNet on cloud (OOF → round-2 targets; members); label lab on the LB; lean one-decode notebook. Day 6–12: round-2 all-data students × 2–3 seeds; sequence head on OOF features; a 448 px CNN family. lens: THE MODEL: what would take a single model from 0.927–0.933 to ≥ 0.950
headline: Our models are short of training signal and compute, not capacity. Every model trains on 12 random windows out of the 54–82 a study has. At eval, a 12-window bag scores 0.048 macro below the full bag (window curve), so for a focal finding 20–50% of positive training bags hold no evidence. On top of that, runs are single-seed with no EMA, every non-Stage-B run used one of its two T4s, and the only main model is a ViT-L that costs ~9 session-hours per all-data run, so its recipe was never tuned. A single checkpoint at ≥0.950 by 10-22 is unlikely. About 0.95 is reachable with three things: full-bag training (or a full-bag head on frozen embeddings), 3–5 seeds or folds of 2–3 families inside our own 9-h notebook (the budget fits about 4 Ortho + 4 CoAtNet at Stage B), and more compute (both T4s, the Mac around the clock, ideally $50–150 of rented A100/H100).

what_went_wrong.title: One of the two T4s sat idle on every Stage A, CNN and CoAtNet run (known since 09-26, still unfixed)
what_went_wrong.evidence: notebooks/build_backbone_ab_kernel.py:326-327 launches a single process unless LAYOUT == 'stage_b' or the arch is qwen. The summary.json files read world 1 or None for ab_coatnet (383 min), ab_ortho (514), c6_ortho (667), dread_ortho (667), coatnet_student_r1_all (456; 63.5 min/epoch) and all five ResNet34 runs: about 48.5 session-hours on one GPU. docs/archive/RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:1138-1142 already says 'Every GPU kernel here has had two T4s and used one.' Two runs were cut short by the 12-h session: dread and c6 Ortho stopped at 8 epochs ('time budget at epoch 7'), against the public core's 16. Kaggle bills the session, not the GPU.
what_went_wrong.cost: About 20 session-hours, two-thirds of a weekly quota. About 10 h of that came after the 09-26 note (dread 11.1 h, CoAtNet student 7.6 h, ResNet runs 2.4 h). The Stage A Ortho models also got half the epochs they could have had.

what_went_wrong.title: 12-window training bags were treated as harmless; the coverage gap at train time was never tested
what_went_wrong.evidence: Training draws k=12 random windows per study (fusion/train_windows.py:280-282) and scores every window at eval. Window curve (docs/archive/RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:1122-1128), c6_ortho trained at k=12: 12 evenly spaced windows −0.0483±0.0044 against 54; 18 windows −0.0142; 36 windows −0.0017. AUDIT.md:186-188 calls the count difference 'harmless for WindowMIL', but that argument covers eval only. Hypergeometric odds that a bag misses a focal finding seen on 6 windows: 20% at Stage A (54 windows, k=12), 34% at Stage B (~76 windows); k=24 brings that to 9%, k=36 to 2%. So Stage B made training bags sparser at fixed k. Each window is seen about 12/82×14 ≈ 2 times over the whole r1 run.
what_went_wrong.cost: Unmeasured. Plausibly 0.005–0.015 on the focal findings (Lateral Meniscus, Lateral OA, PF OA, MCL) in every model trained here, the public core included.

what_went_wrong.title: The small-CNN verdict measured our ViT harness, not the forum's recipe
what_went_wrong.cost: We lost a family that costs 1/40 of Ortho per run (1.9 min/epoch on a T4), and with it cheap seeds, diversity and cheap teachers. The round-1 teacher became the weakest model available, and the round-1 students read about 0 on the LB (CoAtNet 0.931 vs 0.933; Ortho r1 roughly the sum of the known levers). About 1 week.

what_went_wrong.title: Single-seed decisions, with seed noise never measured
what_went_wrong.evidence:
score_oof's paired SE (±0.004–0.005) covers study sampling only. The same recipe on Mac vs Kaggle differed by B′−B = +0.0053 (LOG.md:78-80). Mean per-finding Spearman on the 691, computed here from fusion/runs_*/oof_all.csv:
- ResNet34 B vs C (identical apart from the affine): 0.808.
- ResNet34 B vs Ortho-r1: 0.797, so seed-level disagreement is as large as the architecture gap.
- c6 vs c7: 0.921.
Three levers were closed on single seeds within that noise: zoom (Z−R +0.0070, P 0.943), the affine augmentation (−0.0019) and NYU N (+0.0035). Every run used seed 42.
what_went_wrong.cost: Possibly closed real +0.005-scale levers. It also hid how much seed and fold ensembling is worth.

what_went_wrong.title: The main model is too expensive to iterate on, so its recipe was never tuned
what_went_wrong.evidence: Ortho Stage B trains at 2.525 s per 2-study micro-step per T4, about 105 ms per window (runs_ortho_student_r1 bench.json): 36 min/epoch on 3,502 with DDP and about 8.6 h for an all-data run, so roughly one Ortho experiment per week. Its recipe is the public CoAtNet's: lr, OneCycle 15%, k=12, clip 3.0, intensity-only augmentation (train_windows.py:748). On top sits one Stage B package (llrd 0.9, drop_path 0.1, top lr 9e-5, slot and depth embedding; build_backbone_ab_kernel.py PACKAGE) adopted as a bundle and never ablated. Unchanged in every Ortho run: aug_affine 0.0, no EMA, one seed. The confidence weight 0.25+0.75|2y−1| (train_windows.py:759) was built for steven_v2's 'not said' 0.5. It was kept for dread_soft and the teacher targets, cutting dread_soft's 0.45 level to a third of the weight, and was never A/B'd. The public core has no such weight.
what_went_wrong.cost: Bag size, EMA, augmentation and schedule have never been touched on the main model; plausibly 0.005–0.01.

what_went_wrong.title: The CoAtNet student spent 7.6 session-hours on a null its setup made likely
what_went_wrong.evidence: It started from the converged SWA public core and restarted a full OneCycle at the same 3e-5 peak: loss 0.5756 → 0.5822 at epoch 1 → 0.5536, relative weight change 0.024 (RUNBOOK.md:184-186). It kept Stage A input for core-slot compatibility, so it never got Stage B's +0.014. It trained on the weakest teacher (ResNet34 at 224) on one T4, and read 0.931 vs 0.933.
what_went_wrong.cost: 7.6 session-hours and the weekend's main read.

what_went_wrong.title: Ortho r1 held out the 691 for a read that cannot judge its labels
what_went_wrong.evidence: RUNBOOK rule 3: 'the 691 judges fixed-target comparisons only'. r1 trained on teacher targets with 3,502 studies (−24% data). The public author measured +0.010 from all data (MODEL.md §0), so our best-alone 0.927 lacks it. The fix is today's 8.6-h all-data run.
what_went_wrong.cost: About 0.01 LB on the 10-03 read, and a week.

closed_too_early.title: 'k=12 vs every window is harmless for WindowMIL' (AUDIT.md:186-188)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: The argument covers eval only: the attention pool accepts any window count. Whether 12-window training bags carry enough evidence was never asked, and the evidence says they often don't.
closed_too_early.evidence: Window curve: 12 windows −0.0483, 18 −0.0142, 36 −0.0017 against 54 (archive :1122-1128). Hypergeometric miss rates are 20–34% for a 6-window finding at k=12. The stack's core code gains +0.005 from denser test sampling plus a reversed pass on the same weights (RUNBOOK.md:56).

closed_too_early.title: Small CNN as a main model or family (RUNBOOK Settled, 'Cut: ResNet34 as a main model'; archive :364-368)
closed_too_early.evidence: LOG.md:77-140 (B′ 0.8129, R 0.8218, Z 0.8288); REFERENCE §3.1b (0.94+ at 224–288 px); ResNet34-B vs Ortho-r1 per-finding Spearman 0.797, so a working CNN would add real diversity.

closed_too_early.title: Zoom / crops 'STOPS' (LOG.md:128-140)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: One seed at P 0.943, with seed noise of about ±0.005 (B′ vs B). The crop-specific gains landed on hard findings: MCL +0.052 over R, Lateral OA +0.042 over B′, and Lateral OA is one of the gold weak four. It was never tested on a ViT. For Ortho at 384 a 16-px token covers 5.8 mm, so a zoomed view means finer tokens over the same pixels, which is not the same as 'more resolution'.
closed_too_early.evidence: Z−R +0.0070±0.0045. DATA §10b: thin cartilage and ligaments are smaller than one ViT token; CoAtNet (conv early stages) beat Ortho on Lateral OA (+0.024) and PF OA (+0.022) in runs_ab_ortho/score_vs_coatnet.txt.

closed_too_early.title: 'Augmentation buys nothing' (C vs B −0.0019, archive :364-368)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: Tested on ResNet34 at 224 only, with one seed. The 303M-parameter Ortho and the 74M CoAtNet still train with a ±10% intensity gain as their only augmentation and have never had an augmentation arm.
closed_too_early.evidence: aug_affine 0.0 in every Ortho and CoAtNet summary.json; train_windows.py:748.

closed_too_early.title: Seed/fold ensembling of one family ('worth ~+0.001', MODEL.md:34); avg3 as the only averaging
closed_too_early.why_reopen: Our own OOFs show high run-to-run disagreement, so averaging seeds or folds should pay more than the core author's 3-arm blend on one corpus. avg3 averages the last 3 epochs at an annealed LR, which is not a seed ensemble.
closed_too_early.evidence: Spearman ResNet34 B vs C 0.808 (recipes one flag apart); avg3 moved the 691 by +0.000 to +0.0024 (RUNBOOK Open 5); the public stack is +0.015 over its best member.

closed_too_early.title: 'The blend of our own two models' (RUNBOOK.md:285, Cut)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: It was cut when the second model was a weak ResNet34 (−0.0057 on the 691). The current pair (CoAtNet student 0.931, Ortho student 0.927, soon Ortho all-data) has never had an LB read, and it is final B's core.
closed_too_early.evidence: Ortho-r1 vs ImageNet-CoAtNet per-finding Spearman: 0.797 mean, Baker's 0.574, Lateral OA 0.734, Lateral Meniscus 0.791. Per-finding strengths are complementary (score_vs_coatnet.txt).
