ideas.title: Use the compute already paid for: both T4s on every run, the Mac around the clock, and resume across sessions
ideas.mechanism:
Kaggle bills the session, not the GPU.
- Set NPROC to device_count for stage_a; DDP is already proven on Stage B. For single-GPU arms, run two independent arms or seeds per session with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and 1.
- Add checkpoint and resume (optimizer, scheduler and scaler state saved each epoch to /kaggle/working, with the previous version attached as input) so a schedule is no longer capped at 12 h. dread and c6 were cut to 8 epochs where the core used 16.
- Keep the idle Mac on the CNN and head experiments below every night.
ideas.evidence_for: build_backbone_ab_kernel.py:326-327; 48.5 single-GPU session-hours in fusion/runs_*; c6 and dread stopped at the time budget; the Mac runs ResNet34 at ~5 min/epoch and is free; RUNBOOK 'Running now: nothing'.
ideas.evidence_against: CPU and shard I/O contention for two concurrent arms is unmeasured (data wait is 0.3% for CoAtNet, 6–8% for ResNet34). Confirm the per-session billing on the quota page.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly. Roughly doubles the number of runs and seeds, which feeds the +0.003–0.008 from seeds below.
ideas.cost: About 0.5–1 engineering day; no GPU.
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Next push: CoAtNet at 4,349 should drop from 63.5 to ~33 min/epoch.
ideas.fastest_test: Build the next CoAtNet stage_a run with NPROC=2 (TW_FORCE_CKPT smoke as rule 11). Read 'steps/epoch' halving and identical DDP checksums in the log.

ideas.title: Rent GPU time for training; keep the Kaggle quota for inference and commit runs
ideas.mechanism:
A T4 runs fp16 at roughly 20–25 effective TFLOPs. An A100 runs bf16 at about 150, an H100 at 300+.
- Ortho all-data (8.6 h on 2×T4, ~17 T4-GPU-h) ≈ 2.5–3 A100-h, about $5.
- 4 Ortho teacher folds ≈ $20.
- 3 extra seeds ≈ $15.
It also unlocks k=24–36 bags, 448 px and full 16-epoch schedules that do not fit a 12-h T4 session. Switch autocast to bf16 (train_windows.autocast is hard-coded to fp16 on CUDA). Download the Stage A and B shards (32 + 62 GB) with the kaggle CLI. The infer_windows --check-against gate already proves parity back on Kaggle. A secondary free option is Kaggle's separate TPU quota, but PyTorch/XLA porting of a RoPE ViT-L is risky in 19 days.
ideas.evidence_for: About 64 session-hours of T4×2 remain (~4 now + 30 + ~30), and the plan needs ~20 h for teacher folds alone. The public core trained in bf16 (MODEL.md §0), so its author did not use T4s. Rules: competition data may be used 'for any purpose… including participating' (COMPETITION_RULES.txt:74); winner obligations only require documented training code and environment.
ideas.evidence_against: The owner's budget and preference are unknown. A day of setup. Data-handling duty ('reasonable measures', rules :80). bf16 vs fp16 numerics need one parity check.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Enabler. The levers it makes affordable (folds, seeds, bag size, round 2) plausibly add +0.01–0.02 to the final.
ideas.cost: $50–150 total; about 1 day of setup.
ideas.fastest_test: Rent one A100 or H100 for an hour. Copy one Stage B shard and run 50 Ortho steps with --max-steps at micro 4 in bf16. If it is ≥6× a T4's 2.525 s per 2-study step, move the teacher folds and seeds there.

ideas.title: Fix the training bag: k=12 random windows → k=24–36 or slot-stratified bags (test on the CNN tonight, then port)
ideas.evidence_for: Window curve: 12 windows −0.048, 36 windows −0.0017. 34% of positive bags miss a 6-window finding at Stage B. The forum's CNNs pool every slice. The core gains +0.005 from denser test sampling.
ideas.evidence_against: The 0.928–0.933 public core trains at k=12, so k=12 is not fatal. Fewer distinct study updates per unit of compute could hurt the global findings (Effusion, Synovitis). Port cost is 2–3× per epoch.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.003–0.010, concentrated on Lateral Meniscus, Lateral OA, PF OA and MCL.
ideas.cost: Mac: B′ recipe at k=36 ≈ 15 min/epoch, so 6 epochs ≈ 1.5 h and 18 epochs ≈ 4.5 h, plus the stratified arm at 1.5 h, all free. Port: CoAtNet k=24 ≈ 7.3 session-h for 7 epochs on 2×T4.
ideas.fastest_test: train_windows --arch resnet34 --mps --k 36 --epochs 6 (and 18) on Stage A with dread_soft, the same 3,502 / 691. Pair against B′ 0.8129 with score_oof and report the weak findings. Run 2 seeds of B′ first so seed noise is known.

ideas.title: Full-bag head on frozen r1 embeddings, plus an attention and slot diagnostic (best use of this week's ~4 h)
ideas.evidence_for: Window curve; RSNA 2024 lumbar 1st place used attention MIL plus a bi-LSTM over slices (REFERENCE §4.5); the gold meniscus criterion (REFERENCE §2); a head costs seconds per epoch, so many arms are free.
ideas.evidence_against: Embeddings for the 3,502 are in-sample (the encoder saw those labels), so a re-fitted head may overfit; the 691 shows that. The encoder was tuned for 12-window bags, so head-only gains may be small.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.002–0.006 if it transfers. The diagnostic itself decides whether crops or specialists are worth building.
ideas.cost: About 1.7 session-hours (4,251 studies × 2.9 s / 2 GPUs) and ~0.7 GB of fp16 embeddings; the Mac is free.
ideas.fastest_test: A kernel: r1 last.pt with --epochs 0, saving every window's encoder output for train, 691 and gold. Read paired 691 deltas per head arm.

ideas.title: A second family that pulls its weight: CoAtNet on Stage B (canonical, native 384, 96 slices, slot and depth embedding), from the public init, DDP, all data
ideas.mechanism: The CoAtNet student used Stage A only to fit the stack's core slot. For final B the slot doesn't matter: give CoAtNet the input that bought Ortho +0.014 on the LB. Fine-tune 7–8 epochs from raptor maxspan-v5 on 2×T4. Optionally use k=24 and EMA if the CNN tests pass.
ideas.evidence_for: Stage B +0.0112 on the 691 (runs_c7_ortho/score_runs_ortho.txt), +0.014 on the LB. CoAtNet beats Ortho on Lateral OA (+0.024), PF OA (+0.022), MCL and Fracture (runs_ab_ortho/score_vs_coatnet.txt), two of the gold weak four. Ortho-r1 vs CoAtNet per-finding Spearman 0.797 (Baker's 0.57, Lateral OA 0.73). Training costs 72 ms/window vs Ortho's 105.
ideas.evidence_against: Fine-tuning the core on new targets moved nothing (0.931 vs 0.933). The init's features and BN statistics come from upsampled, non-canonical input. The init saw the 691, so only the LB can judge.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Alone about 0.935–0.945. Equal-rank with Ortho all-data, +0.005–0.010 over the better of the two.
ideas.cost: About 4.5 session-hours (≈32 min/epoch at 4,349 on DDP × 8, plus eval); inference ≈ 16 min per model on 2×T4.
ideas.time_to_first_signal: One session plus a commit run (~1 day).
ideas.fastest_test: build_backbone_ab_kernel --arch coatnet --corpus stage_b --all-data --train-args '--init …maxspan… --epochs 8'. Read alone through --ours-only, paired against 0.931.

ideas.title: Seeds and folds inside our own 9-h notebook (final B), one shared decode, and the stack's dense + reversed inference for any Stage A CoAtNet
ideas.mechanism:
Final B owes nothing to the stack's 8–9 h runtime.
- Ortho Stage B costs 2.88 s/study/T4, about 32 min per model on 2×T4. A Stage B CoAtNet ≈ 16 min. Stage B decode ≈ 31 min once (b=3.8 s/study/worker × 1.5, archive :1119).
- So 4 Ortho + 4 CoAtNet plus TTA fit in about 4–5 h. infer_windows needs to decode once and run N checkpoints.
- Any Stage A CoAtNet must go through the stack's core code (≤96 slices plus a reversed pass), worth +0.005 on the same weights (RUNBOOK.md:56), not through infer_windows' 64 slices.
ideas.evidence_for: Near-identical ResNet recipes rank-correlate at only 0.81; the stack is +0.015 over its best member; the hidden-test rerun costs no quota.
ideas.evidence_against: The core author: same-family blends worth ~+0.001 (MODEL.md:34). Each extra Ortho seed costs 8.6 session-h on T4s.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.004–0.010 for 3–4 Ortho models vs 1; +0.005 for the CoAtNet run through the stack's core code.
ideas.cost: About 1 engineering day for multi-model inference; training per extra Ortho seed 8.6 session-h (or ~$5 rented).
ideas.fastest_test: A free 2-model ensemble already exists: r1 (3,502) + Ortho all-data (4,349). Submit their average through --ours-only next to all-data alone. One commit run, no training.

ideas.title: Ortho k-fold as a triple-use investment, not just a teacher
ideas.evidence_for: On gold: report + Ortho OOF 0.9216–0.927 vs report + ResNet34 0.913 (DATA §12 item 2; archive :640 table). A strong teacher dilutes less than a weak one (Ortho + pilkwang < Ortho alone).
ideas.evidence_against: Round 1 bought ~0 to +0.005 on the LB. Fold models train on 3/4 of the data, so each is weaker than all-data. Gold can only gate one teacher variant (AUDIT open question 3).
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Round-2 student +0.003–0.008; the fold ensemble at test +0.003–0.007.
ideas.cost: About 5.1 session-hours per fold (≈34 min/epoch × 8 + eval of ~1,090 held-out studies), so ~20.5 h, or ~$20 rented.
ideas.time_to_first_signal: About 1 week on T4s (the 10-09 reset); about 1 day rented.
ideas.fastest_test: Pre-register the gold gate against round 1's 0.913. Make each fold also save last.pt and the per-window embeddings for its held-out fold and for gold.

ideas.title: Dense-slice TTA for Stage B models
ideas.mechanism: Add a 'c7-dense' spec: the same 7 slots with about 1.5× the slices each, built from DICOMs at inference. window_meta's relative depth keeps the slot and depth embedding meaningful, and the attention pool accepts any count. It mainly fills in the coronal and axial slots (Stage B keeps 16 of ~30 coronal and 14 of ~32 axial slices, DATA §10b).
ideas.evidence_for: The window curve was still rising from 36 to 54 windows (+0.0017). The stack's core gains +0.005 from ≤96 slices plus a reversed pass on the same weights.
ideas.evidence_against: Sagittal is already nearly complete at Stage B. Inference is decode-bound, so decode grows about 1.5× (~45 min). The depth embedding was learned on fixed slot sizes.
ideas.cost: About 20 lines (a new SPECS entry plus a load_meta bypass); about 0.7 session-hours to read on the 691 from DICOMs.
ideas.fastest_test: infer_windows on the 691 with r1 weights, spec c7 vs c7-dense. Paired with score_oof (fixed model and targets, so the 691 is a valid judge).

ideas.title: EMA of weights in every run
ideas.mechanism: Keep an exponential moving average of the weights (decay ≈ 0.999 per optimizer step, about a 2-epoch horizon) and evaluate and ship the EMA weights. For Ortho, hold it on the CPU and update every 4–8 steps: peak GPU memory is 14.5 of 15 GB (runs_ortho_student_r1 bench.json). CoAtNet and the CNNs can hold it on the GPU.
ideas.evidence_for: Fine-tuning on noisy labels usually gains from weight averaging. The public core ships a gold-picked top-3 SWA. Our avg3 (last 3 epochs at near-zero LR) is a weak proxy that still read +0.000 to +0.0024.
ideas.evidence_against: OneCycle's anneal already averages somewhat; the gain may sit below seed noise.
ideas.cost: About 30 lines; ~1–2% step time for Ortho.
ideas.fastest_test: B′ recipe ± EMA on the Mac, 2 seeds each, paired on the 691. Then make it the default for every later run.

ideas.title: Build the fast CNN family properly at 384 (the forum's 0.94+ recipe in our input)
ideas.evidence_for: Forum 0.94+ (REFERENCE §3.1b). R +0.0089 and Z +0.0159 show the CNN was resolution-starved. CNN-specific defects in our setup: BatchNorm over 2 knees per micro-batch, train_windows.py:374 without antialias. RSNA 2024 lumbar found ConvNeXt-S/EffNetV2-S beat ViTs (REFERENCE §4.5). Diversity: the CNN's rank correlation with Ortho is 0.80.
ideas.evidence_against: The affine arm was null; 'the ceiling is what the features can see' (archive :367); the archive's 9e saw five encoders in one band; a CNN at 384 is about 6× ResNet34@224 per window.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Single about 0.925–0.935; as a third family in final B, +0.003–0.008.
ideas.cost: Mac sweep free over 2–3 days; then about 9 session-hours for 5 seeds at 384.
ideas.fastest_test: Mac, Stage A: B′ vs B′ with --micro 8 vs B′ with a GeM/mean+max head vs B′ at 336 with antialias, 2 seeds each, paired on the 691.

ideas.title: Per-finding spatial attention (dense MIL) for the cartilage findings
ideas.mechanism: Replace the in-window global average (CoAtNet's 12×12 or ResNet's 11×11 final map) with per-finding attention over window × spatial cells. For Ortho, use patch tokens instead of the CLS token only. A 2–3 mm cartilage defect is 1 of ~144 cells and is diluted by an average pool. Pair it with a zoomed view (the centre 94 mm) for the joint-line findings.
ideas.evidence_for: Owner Q&A 09-28 (archive :249) already named it as 'a small head change'. Lateral OA moved +0.042 with zoom on the CNN, and conv features beat ViT on Lateral OA and PF OA. Lateral OA and PF OA are 2 of the gold weak four.
ideas.evidence_against: Never measured. Deep features have large receptive fields, so dilution may already be learned around. The public core uses avg pooling and reads 0.928. Attention can collapse onto artifacts.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.002–0.008 macro, mostly Lateral OA and PF OA.
ideas.cost: About 40 lines; one Mac arm (ResNet34@336 ≈ 3 h); a CoAtNet port of about 4.5 session-hours if it passes.
ideas.fastest_test: R (ResNet34@336, 0.8218) vs R with a dense per-finding attention head, 2 seeds, paired on the 691, reading Lateral OA and PF OA.

ideas.title: Mirror-swap augmentation for the lateral findings (unconventional)
ideas.mechanism: On canonical Stage B, randomly mirror a study: reverse the sagittal slice order and depth, flip coronal and axial columns. Then swap the Medial↔Lateral Meniscus and Medial↔Lateral OA targets, and mask the MCL loss (no LCL label). The lateral heads gain the far more common medial positives as extra examples.
ideas.evidence_for: Lateral Meniscus and Lateral OA are both in the gold weak four. Their medial twins are strong (691 r1: Medial Meniscus 0.909 vs Lateral 0.869; Medial OA 0.868 vs Lateral 0.803). No flip has ever been used here, because a flip without the label swap breaks laterality.
ideas.evidence_against: The knee is not mirror-symmetric (O-shaped lateral meniscus, popliteus hiatus, fibula), so a mirrored medial knee is a synthetic 'lateral' knee and may teach artifacts. The depth embedding semantics change.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: −0.002 to +0.004 macro; high variance.
ideas.cost: About 30 lines; a CNN test needs the Stage B cache locally (62 GB) or about 2 T4-hours.
ideas.fastest_test: Fast CNN at Stage B, mirror p=0.3 vs off, 2 seeds, reading Lateral Meniscus and Lateral OA on the 691.

winner_would: Treat compute as the binding constraint. Rent an A100/H100 for training (about $100 covers folds, seeds and k=36) and spend Kaggle quota on commit runs. At minimum, never leave a T4 or the Mac idle, and add resume so schedules are not capped at 12 h.

Screen the training recipe on a cheap proxy (the CNN on the Mac or a T4) with 2 seeds per arm, then port only the winners (bag size, head, EMA, augmentation) to Ortho and CoAtNet. Today the main model's recipe is copied, not tuned.
Train on (near-)full bags, or go two-stage: fine-tune the encoder, then train the aggregator, with sequence context and per-finding attention, on every window's embedding.
Run 5 folds of the main recipe once and use them three ways: OOF teacher targets for round 2, leak-free embeddings for the stage-2 head, and a fold ensemble at test.

Make final B 2–3 strong, diverse families (Ortho ViT-L, a Stage B CoAtNet, a fixed fast CNN) × 3–5 seeds or folds at equal rank, using the full 9 h. Never add a weaker member at 1/3 to someone else's stack.
Ship EMA weights. Measure dense-slice TTA once on the 691. Run any Stage A CoAtNet through the stack's dense + reversed core code (+0.005).
Measure seed noise once (two seeds of one recipe) and refuse to close a lever whose effect is smaller than that noise.
Put gold-58 into the final all-data training (×3–5), finals only: they are the only labels drawn the way the test is graded.

Aim architecture work at the gold weak four: local pooling or a zoom view for cartilage (Lateral OA, PF OA), canonical depth plus a sequence head for Lateral Meniscus, a stronger image teacher for Synovitis. Stop spending runs on findings already at 0.93–0.99.

lens: THE LABELS: how to get training targets closer to the radiologists' image grades
headline: The teacher-to-student gate measured the wrong thing. On gold-58, "report + image teacher" (+0.026) is an ensemble that includes the report, and test studies have no report. A teacher trained on the same report labels can only teach E[report | image], which a student learns anyway. That is why the students read flat both on gold (Ortho student 0.911 vs dread 0.912, even with Stage B added; CoAtNet 0.9192 vs 0.9187) and on the LB (0.931 vs 0.933; 0.927 vs about 0.930 if the levers added). The one label change that moved the LB (+0.015, dread_soft) added new information about where the graders draw the line. Its stronger version, a frontier LLM reading all 4,407 reports against the official criteria (~$60–150), was planned on 09-06 and never run. Recommendation: move label effort from GPU-hours on same-label teachers to API dollars on grader-side information. Bundle the fixes into one target set and judge it with free Mac-trained students on the LB.

what_went_wrong.title: The label gate scored a report-plus-image ensemble that cannot exist at test time
what_went_wrong.evidence: build_student_targets.py:13-18 and :137: the target is the mean of the report level and the teacher (mapped onto the base). The gate (docs/archive/RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:542) scored those TARGETS as predictors on gold: 0.8873 -> 0.9132, P 0.994. The students trained on them read flat. From fusion/runs_*/summary.json gold_macro_report_only: c6 (Stage A, steven_v2) 0.8777 -> c7 (Stage B, steven_v2) 0.8897, so Stage B alone is worth about +0.012 on gold. Yet dread (Stage A, dread_soft) 0.9121 -> Ortho student (Stage B + teacher targets) 0.9111, which puts the teacher at about -0.01 on gold. CoAtNet student 0.9192 vs public start 0.9187. On the LB: 0.931 vs 0.933, and 0.927 vs about 0.930 if the levers added (RUNBOOK.md:63). Gold-58 does work as an instrument when it scores a STUDENT: c6 -> dread +0.034 on gold matched +0.015 on the LB. A gate of this shape cannot fail: every decent image teacher adds to the report as a predictor (pilkwang aside: +0.003).
what_went_wrong.cost: ~17 GPU-h (CoAtNet student 7.4 h, Ortho student ~10 h, part of it also bought Stage B and all-data value), 4.7 Mac-h of CNN teachers, ~5 days. Plan item (1) would spend ~20 more GPU-h (2/3 of a week) under the same gate, which will pass (report + Ortho OOF already reads 0.9216–0.927) and predicts nothing.

what_went_wrong.title: The frontier-LLM criteria read was planned, costed and never run; a 9B 4-bit local model was tested instead and the route was closed by analogy
what_went_wrong.evidence: DATA.md §6–§7: Opus batch $60–150, Stage L scheduled Sep 7–15, with the official criteria verbatim, structured outputs and a mention mask. extractor/llm_extract.py still carries the older 5-state schema, never submitted. extractor/qwen_label.py:45 ran Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit with no thinking, scored from next-token letters. Result (DATA.md:530-535): -0.0108 overall, frozen six -0.039, but Fracture +0.108. docs/archive/RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:519 says the route 'stays unrun: every reader reads the same text'. Two days later dread_soft, a better-graded reading of the same text, gave +0.015 LB.
what_went_wrong.cost: The only label lever that costs dollars rather than GPU sat idle for ~4 weeks. Plausible LB left on the table: +0.003 to +0.010 single model.

what_went_wrong.title: The teacher was weaker than the student, the students were not noised, and the CoAtNet student was a short fine-tune from a converged SWA checkpoint
what_went_wrong.evidence: CNN teacher mean of 4 folds on the 691: 0.832 (archive :542), vs the Ortho student's 0.853 (fusion/runs_ortho_student_r1/score_runs_ortho.txt). CoAtNet student summary.json: drop_path 0.0, aug_affine 0.0, 7 epochs, init = public SWA; relative weight change 0.024 (RUNBOOK). Ortho student: drop_path 0.1, aug_affine 0. Noisy Student / born-again gains need a teacher at least as strong as the student, a student trained with noise, and enough steps to leave the old basin. Round 1 met none of these.
what_went_wrong.cost: Round 1 could not show a gain even if the mechanism works. So the null is uninformative about Ortho-strength teachers, and 20 GPU-h is being decided by forecast.

what_went_wrong.title: No control isolates the teacher's LB effect
what_went_wrong.evidence: Stage B + dread_soft without a teacher was never trained. 0.927 (Stage B + teacher targets) is compared with an additive forecast of ~0.930 (RUNBOOK.md:63), with ±0.005–0.008 noise. The Mac could have run the equivalent ResNet34 pair for free.
what_went_wrong.cost: The decision on the plan's most expensive item (Ortho k-fold, ~20 GPU-h) rests on inference, not measurement.

what_went_wrong.title: The label instrument's iteration tier was never built
what_went_wrong.evidence: DATA.md §3 designs two tiers: 303 hand-read studies for iteration, gold-58 as arbiter. labeling/model_labels.csv has 86 rows (L1 '217 of 303' never finished, DATA.md §7). So every reader decision has had to spend gold-58 (≤3 candidates) or an LB read.
what_went_wrong.cost: No cheap way to iterate a prompt; this made the frontier read look riskier than it is.

what_went_wrong.title: The LB, the only large image-graded set, was barely used for labels
what_went_wrong.evidence: 5 submissions/day, about 95 left before 10-22. The hidden-test rerun is off-quota; only the ~6-minute commit run counts (RUNBOOK Open item 4). One LB read decided the biggest label question (dread_soft, +0.015). Mac students (free, about 1 h each) have never been submitted. The public LB is ~400 graded studies x 12 findings, about 7x gold-58.
what_went_wrong.cost: Roughly 10–20 label reads that could have run since 09-28 at about 0.1 GPU-h each.

what_went_wrong.title: Fixes tested one at a time below the instrument's resolution
what_went_wrong.evidence: DATA.md §12 item 8: 'No instrument can confirm a one-finding fix: +0.03 on one finding is +0.0025 macro, and a paired LB read resolves ±0.005'. The Synovitis fix, the OA compartment fix and the extra report outputs are each a one-finding or few-finding change.
what_went_wrong.cost: Each small but principled fix returns a null and never ships, even though their sum could be detectable.

what_went_wrong.title: The Synovitis silence fix was judged with a circular teacher
what_went_wrong.evidence: DATA.md:662-672. In dread_soft, Synovitis is a fill derived from Effusion in 3,751 of 4,349 cells. The ResNet34 teacher that replaced those cells was itself trained on that fill, so it imputes 'effusion-ness'. Result 0.824 vs 0.833, recorded as NOT SUPPORTED.
what_went_wrong.cost: A valid construct-confusion fix (synovitis is not effusion; graders couple them at 0.63/0.22, reports at 0.92/0.01) was closed.

what_went_wrong.title: Gold-58 spent on exploratory reads
what_went_wrong.evidence: docs/archive/RUNBOOK-2026-09-28.md:634 (7-arm 'TEACHERS ON GOLD' table, not pre-registered), plus the Qwen, NYU, CNN-gate and synovitis reads. AUDIT.md open Q3 flags exactly this.
what_went_wrong.cost: Every later gold number carries ~+0.003–0.005 of selection optimism (the project's own estimate for a 3-way pick); the arbiter is wearing out.

closed_too_early.title: Frontier LLM (Opus/Sonnet 5.5 class) graded read with the official criteria
closed_too_early.why_reopen: The closing argument (same text, LLM-to-LLM r 0.82, ~0.90 ceiling) was about mention-detectors. Two pieces of evidence point the other way. dread_soft, a better grading of the same text, gave +0.015 on the LB. A criteria-aware reader is a different reader (Qwen Spearman 0.72 with steven_v2), and it lost only where a 9B 4-bit model is weak (ACL/MCL). Gold-58 IS a valid paired instrument for a single reader (SD 0.0042); the ensemble artifact does not apply to a single text source. The hand read's reading-skill headroom is +0.055 [+0.005, +0.111] (DATA.md §1). Cost is dollars and runs alongside GPU work.

ideas.title: A label instrument that scores STUDENTS on image truth: Mac ResNet34 students to gold-58 and the LB, calibrated on the known +0.015
ideas.mechanism: A label change only matters through the model trained on it. Train the cheap recipe-C ResNet34 (224 px, Stage A, 17 epochs, ~70 min on the M5) on each candidate target file. Score the STUDENT on gold-58 (paired, pre-registered) and on the LB through --ours-only (paired vs the same recipe on dread_soft, ±0.005). Calibrate first: steven_v2 vs dread_soft with this student should reproduce a clear gain (+0.008 or more LB) if the instrument transfers. infer_windows builds from meta['timm'] (infer_windows.py:120), so resnet34 should already be servable.
ideas.evidence_for: Gold scoring students tracked the LB in all three measured cases: labels +0.034 gold / +0.015 LB; Stage B +0.012 / +0.014; teacher about -0.01 / about -0.003. B′ on the Mac matched Kaggle's run of the same recipe (docs/LOG.md 09-28 21:35), so Mac students are trustworthy. Hidden reruns are off-quota. 22nd/85th place validate one change at a time this way.
ideas.evidence_against: A weak student (~0.81 on the 691, LB maybe ~0.88–0.90) may react to labels differently from CoAtNet/Ortho. LB reads carry public-LB selection risk, controlled by pre-registered adopt-if-≥ rules. The --ours-only path has never served a ResNet.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly; it is the precondition for every label decision below and could prevent ~20 wasted GPU-h
ideas.cost: ~2.5 Mac-h, 2 submissions (~0.2 GPU-h commit runs), ≤0.5 day to confirm the resnet34 serve path
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Gold read tonight; LB read Sun 10-04
ideas.fastest_test: Tonight: train recipe C on steven_v2 and on dread_soft (dread_soft may reuse B′/C if the recipe matches exactly), score both students on gold-58, then submit both --ours-only on Sunday. Pre-register: the instrument is VALID iff the LB delta is ≥ +0.008 with the sign of the Ortho result.

ideas.title: Frontier criteria-graded read of all 4,407 reports (Claude Opus 5.5 via Batch), DATA.md §4 schema plus location and status fields
ideas.mechanism: Give the reader the official cut-points verbatim, plus 'borderline = negative'. Per finding it returns: mentioned; the graded quantity the criterion names (effusion size; ACL fibre %; meniscus signal surface-contact vs intrasubstance, morphology; per-compartment cartilage depth and extent; MCL grade and ACUTE vs chronic; fracture acuity; per-lesion contusion vs fracture line; Baker's size); p_above; location (compartment, horn, condyle/plateau/patella); post-operative status (ACL graft, meniscectomy); a short evidence quote. Adaptive thinking at effort medium, structured outputs, read in the native language (61% non-English). Use: (i) as a second reader rank-averaged with dread_soft and mapped onto dread_soft's levels; (ii) as the source of severity, location and mention fields for the ideas below.
ideas.evidence_for: dread_soft's threshold-step grading gave +0.015 LB, the largest label effect measured. Qwen-9B with the criteria read Fracture +0.108 better on gold (DATA.md:530-535). The hand read adds +0.055 [+0.005, +0.111] over shipped tables (DATA.md §1). Turkish and Croatian public reads over-call 21–22% (DATA.md §2), where a frontier multilingual reader is strongest. 71st place used an API reader. Commercial LLMs are permitted (REFERENCE.md §1.1).
ideas.evidence_against: Part of the report-vs-image gap is not in the text at all (DATA.md §12: 'moderate effusion' read negative by graders). The frozen six (ACL 0.993 etc.) have no headroom. LLM readers correlate. It cannot be compared with dread_soft on gold (dread_soft has no gold rows). Qwen failed.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: As a reader: gold +0.010 to +0.030 vs steven_v2. Student LB: +0.003 to +0.010 single model; ~0.4x that in the stack, and only if the core is re-fit on it
ideas.cost: Opus 5.5 Batch ($2/$10 per Mtok at 50% off): 5.2M input tokens (~$11, system block cached) + ~7–13M output tokens (~$70–130), so ~$80–140. Sonnet 5.5 Batch about half. Pilot of 250 reports ~$5–8. ~1 day engineering (llm_extract.py exists, but its schema must become DATA.md §4's).
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Gold-58 reader read within ~24 h of starting; LB student read ~48 h
ideas.fastest_test: Freeze the prompt using only the 86 hand-read and ~100 random NON-gold reports. Run it on the 58 gold reports (~$2). Pre-registered gate: frontier p_above vs steven_v2, paired on gold-58, ≥ +0.010 with CI > 0 and no finding more than 0.02 down (DATA.md §3 Stage L gate, one candidate). On a pass, run the full batch and feed it into idea 4's bundle.

ideas.title: Decisive equal-strength self-distillation test on the Mac BEFORE any Ortho k-fold
ideas.mechanism: Round 1 paired a weak teacher with a strong student. The CNN round-1 targets come from ResNet34 recipe-C folds, so a ResNet34 recipe-C student on targets_round1_cnn.csv is exactly teacher = student strength. Compare it with the same student on dread_soft. Add a Noisy-Student arm: --aug-affine 1 plus drop_path, and teacher-only targets instead of the 50/50 mean. If equal-strength self-distillation does not move a ResNet on gold-students and the LB, an Ortho round 2 will not move Ortho.
ideas.evidence_for: Born-again / Noisy Student theory needs teacher ≥ student and a noised student; round 1 had neither. 36th place said 'my OOF predictions were already closer to the radiologists than the extracted labels' and used them. 71st gained +0.011 with multi-source teachers.
ideas.evidence_against: A teacher trained on the same labels converges to E[report | image]; the only gain is variance reduction. Round 1 on Ortho read ~0 on gold and on the LB.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Decides the plan's ~20 GPU-h item. If it is positive (≥ +0.008 LB on the ResNet), round 2 is worth +0.003 to +0.008 on Ortho; otherwise those GPU-h go to finals
ideas.cost: ~2.5 Mac-h (2 arms; the dread_soft control is shared with idea 1), 1–2 submissions
ideas.fastest_test: Recipe C on targets_round1_cnn.csv (sha 75757be8) vs recipe C on dread_soft, same 3,502, seed 42. Pre-register: the teacher family continues iff the LB paired delta is ≥ +0.008 (or gold-student ≥ +0.015 with P ≥ 0.95).

ideas.title: targets_v2 as ONE bundle: multi-reader rank-mean, gold-calibrated levels, mention-masked U-SelfTrained for low-mention findings
ideas.mechanism: Effects of +0.002–0.004 each sit below the ±0.005 resolution, so ship them together and test once. (a) Per finding, the rank-mean of dread_soft, the frontier read, steven_v2/v4 and jev_text, mapped onto dread_soft's levels so the threshold step is kept; this averages reader-specific misreads. (b) Levels set to P(grader positive | reader grade), estimated on gold-58 with a few shared parameters (monotone, pooled across findings). This is AUC-invariant within a finding, so it does not spend gold's ranking power. It only changes where BCE spends its effort, which is the hypothesised reason dread_soft won. (c) For cells the report never mentions (Synovitis 87.6%, Fracture ~55%, Contusion ~21% per the Qwen/frontier mention mask), drop the fill. Impute from a teacher trained with those cells masked (--allow-missing-labels), so it is not circular.
ideas.evidence_for: Forum LB evidence: 64th '+0.015 from combining labels', 71st +0.011. dread_soft's step at the threshold. CheXpert: U-SelfTrained works, U-Ignore does not (REFERENCE.md §4.1). Synovitis is an Effusion fill in 3,751 of 4,349 cells. The weakest findings (Synovitis, PF OA, Lateral OA, Lateral Meniscus 0.81–0.87 on gold) are where construct confusions live; +0.05 on those four = +0.017 macro (RUNBOOK.md:191-197).
ideas.evidence_against: The public readers are near-duplicates (r 0.87–0.95). Gold-fitted levels use 58 studies (noisy, some selection). OA severity is often simply absent from the text (DATA.md §12 item 8b), which no reader fixes.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.003 to +0.012 single model; +0.001 to +0.005 in the stack if the core is re-fit
ideas.cost: $0 beyond idea 2; ~1 day to build; ~5 Mac-h if (c) needs 4 masked ResNet teacher folds; 1–2 submissions
ideas.fastest_test: Build targets_v2 = (a)+(b)+(c) and freeze it. One recipe-C student vs the dread_soft student, paired on the LB. Pre-register adopt iff ≥ +0.008; gold-student reported only.

ideas.title: LLM-adjudicated confident learning: the image model flags, the LLM re-reads
ideas.mechanism: Stop averaging every cell toward a weaker teacher. Take the ~5% of cells per finding where the OOF image model disagrees most with dread_soft (the .audit.csv build_student_targets already writes). Ask the frontier model a targeted question per report and finding: does the text support this level under the official criterion (trace? chronic? intrasubstance? lateral patellar facet vs lateral compartment?). If it is a reading error, fix the level from the text. If the report is clear and the image model disagrees (report ≠ image), set ~0.5. Otherwise keep the base. This changes about 5% of the cells instead of all 52k.
ideas.evidence_for: Confident learning (cleanlab) changes only confident disagreements (REFERENCE.md §4.5). Averaging injects teacher noise into the ~85% of cells where the report was right. The project's own OA review found Qwen confusing the lateral patellar facet, a reading error a targeted re-read catches (DATA.md:673-680).
ideas.evidence_against: With a teacher trained on the same labels, the flagged cells are partly teacher errors. The effect is small and concentrated, so it needs bundling.
ideas.cost: ~2,600 targeted calls, ~$10–25; half a day
ideas.fastest_test: Fold it into targets_v2 as component (d). Report the share of flagged cells the LLM calls a 'reading error' vs 'report ≠ image'; if under 20% are reading errors, drop it.

ideas.title: Put gold-58 into the final training (weight 3–5), pre-registered by prior
ideas.mechanism: These are the only labels drawn by the graders on the images. At weight w they are 58w of about 4,349 + 58w effective examples. They teach the graders' thresholds on exactly the borderline cases where reports disagree (FP 25 vs FN 17 in the forum audit, REFERENCE.md §1.4). Finals already use fixed epochs and last/avg3 weights, so no gold-based selection is lost.
ideas.evidence_for: Host: the image label is authoritative and readers are stricter (REFERENCE.md §1.4). Gold Fracture prevalence is 18/58, while the reports' 'meets' is about 3%: the graders see what reports do not say. Free in compute.
ideas.evidence_against: 58 studies, so the expected effect is small and cannot be measured at LB resolution (±0.005). Overfitting at high weight. The finals lose gold as a sanity read.
ideas.cost: ~0.5 day: a --train-gold-weight flag, and relaxing the train∩gold refusal for finals only; 0 extra GPU
ideas.fastest_test: Decide now by prior, w = 3. Check on the Mac that a recipe-C student with gold at w = 3 does not degrade the 691 (a fixed-target sanity check), then apply it to every final run.

ideas.title: Training-only auxiliary outputs from the same frontier pass: where, post-op status, extra findings
ideas.mechanism: Add heads for compartment and horn location, ACL graft present, prior meniscectomy, PCL, LCL, per-compartment cartilage grade, osteophytes, and degenerative vs traumatic marrow oedema. Ignore them at test. They separate constructs the 12 labels mix: a post-meniscectomy truncated meniscus can be grader-positive by morphology while the report says 'post-surgical'; subchondral degenerative oedema is not a contusion; lateral facet is not lateral compartment.
ideas.evidence_for: 86–100% of positive English reports name a sub-location (DATA.md §12 item 5). The main targets stay fixed, so the 691 CAN judge it (rule 3). Lateral OA and MCL are vision-and-locale gaps (zoom MCL +0.052).
ideas.evidence_against: Study-level aux heads do not force spatial attention. Aux-task gains in medical imaging are usually small. Needs trainer changes.
ideas.cost: ~1 day trainer work; 1 Mac run (~1.2 h) judged on the 691
ideas.fastest_test: Recipe C plus aux heads vs recipe C, same dread_soft main targets. The 691 paired gain must be ≥ 0 at P ≥ 0.95 (the 691 is valid because the main targets are fixed).

ideas.title: Strong-teacher pseudo-labels on the 7,140 NYU knees: the public core labels them on the Mac
ideas.mechanism: Distillation with a teacher that never saw these knees and is far stronger than the ResNet that made arm N's labels. The NYU Stage A cache already exists. Run the public maxspan-v5 CoAtNet (+ reversed pass) over it on MPS, then train a student on the 4,349 + 7,140 knees.
ideas.evidence_for: N with a weak teacher was +0.0035 (P 0.75), positive. More real knees gave +0.010 (3,200 -> 4,349). The ensemble-distillation-on-unlabelled-data recipe is standard.
ideas.evidence_against: It teaches E[report | image] at most, not the graders' thresholds. Students cost 2.6x the compute. fastMRI's redistribution terms for a CC BY-NC winner are unread (REFERENCE.md §1.3).
ideas.cost: ~3–5 Mac-h to label (estimate); 1 recipe-C student on the Mac (~3 h); a license check
ideas.fastest_test: Re-run arm N with the public-core pseudo-labels in place of the CNN mean, same rule (691 paired vs B′, P ≥ 0.95). Only do this if the owner clears the license question.

ideas.title: Reconstruct dread_soft's gold rows
ideas.mechanism: dread_soft has no gold rows, so no new reader can be compared with the incumbent on gold. If its generation pipeline (model, prompt, level map) is public, running it on the 58 gold reports gives a paired gold read of the incumbent.
ideas.evidence_for: bench_public_labels.py already runs the paired machinery. AUDIT.md open Q1 asks whether dread_soft was tuned on gold.
ideas.evidence_against: The pipeline may be private or depend on a model we cannot run.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly; makes idea 2's gate 'beats the incumbent' rather than 'beats steven_v2'
ideas.cost: ~1 h plus cents if public
ideas.fastest_test: Owner checks dreaddevelopment's label notebook or dataset page for the prompt.

ideas.title: Ortho k-fold round 2 (plan item 1), only if idea 3 is positive; then treat it as a 5-fold ensemble
ideas.mechanism: Equal-strength OOF for every study, then round-2 targets. The 5 fold models double as an ensemble for final B.
ideas.evidence_for: Report + Ortho OOF reads 0.9216 on gold vs 0.913 for round 1 (archive :634).
ideas.evidence_against: That gate is the ensemble artifact. Round 1 students were flat. ~20 GPU-h is ~2/3 of a week, competing with all-data finals and with re-fitting the core.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.000 to +0.005 from the labels (more if the ensemble ships)
ideas.cost: ~20 GPU-h
ideas.fastest_test: Do not start it until idea 3 reads. The gate must be a student-on-gold or LB read, not report + teacher.

ideas.title: Absorb report bias with a site/language term during training and drop it at test (unconventional)
ideas.mechanism: The training logit is z(image) + b[site or language, finding]; the test logit is z(image). The bias term soaks up systematic report tendencies (Turkish and Croatian over-call 21–22%; site-specific report styles), so the image head z is not pushed to learn site cues as findings. The test is graded by the same strict readers for every site.
ideas.evidence_for: Language agreement ranges 0.78–0.93 (DATA.md §2). Site leakage probe 0.053. Annotator-noise layers are standard in crowd-label learning.
ideas.evidence_against: The site prior died (-0.0057) and ComBat hurt (-0.013 to -0.032): sites differ in real case mix, and the bias term can absorb real prevalence too.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: +0.000 to +0.005 (speculative)
ideas.cost: ~0.5 day; 1 Mac run; 1 submission
ideas.fastest_test: Recipe C with a per-(language, finding) bias in training only (12 x 9 parameters) vs recipe C, paired on the LB; adopt iff ≥ +0.008.

winner_would: Judge every label change by a STUDENT on image truth (gold-58 student reads plus paired LB reads), never by scoring the targets themselves as predictors.
Keep one free, cheap student pipeline (Mac ResNet34) whose only job is label A/Bs on the LB, and spend 2–3 of the 5 daily submissions on it. About 95 remain; hidden reruns are free.

Spend API dollars before GPU-hours. In the first days, run a frontier multilingual reader with the official criteria verbatim and structured graded fields (size, acuity, surface contact, compartment, mention, post-op), and rank-average it with dread_soft instead of replacing it.

Bundle small principled fixes (multi-reader average, gold-calibrated levels, mention-masked imputation for Synovitis/Fracture/Contusion, LLM-adjudicated flips) into one targets_v2. Test it once; ship it if it is +0.008 or more paired.
Use self-distillation only with teacher ≥ student, a noised student, and enough steps. Test that on the cheap model before buying Ortho k-fold.

lens: Compute, operating cadence and rules (the resource side of winning)
headline: Compute is the binding constraint, and the limit is one the project set itself. On Kaggle alone there is exactly one more label iteration before 10-22: the 4-fold Ortho teacher by itself takes ~20 of next week's 30 quota-hours. The same work costs ~$5–25 on one rented H100, and a winner-scale program (~400–600 T4-hours) costs ~$50–200. No rule forbids training off Kaggle. The leaderboard is the only instrument that scores against the radiologists' image labels, and its scoring rerun does not use quota. The project has used it ~13 times in ~55 days because of a stale belief that each submission costs ~2 GPU-hours. A winner would keep every machine busy around the clock and make 3–5 pre-registered leaderboard reads a day.

what_went_wrong.evidence: Kaggle charges quota per session-hour, not per GPU. At 08:25 on 10-03, 12 h 50 min were left (RUNBOOK.md:72) after the CoAtNet student (wall 456 min on one T4, fusion/runs_coatnet_student_r1_all/runs_coatnet/summary.json: world 1, 63.8 min/epoch) and the Ortho student (wall 546 min on two T4s, fusion/runs_ortho_student_r1/runs_ortho/summary.json). That is ~17.2 h used. Charging per GPU would have meant ~33 h, which is more than the 30 h quota. So every session already buys two T4s. AUDIT.md:255-257 flagged it on 09-26, and the CoAtNet student still ran on one GPU a week later.

closed_too_early.title: 'No cloud GPUs' (owner, 09-27)
closed_too_early.why_reopen: The price is tiny compared with what the quota costs in calendar time. Ortho Stage B costs ~1.26 T4-seconds per study-epoch (0.105 s/window × 12 windows). So the 4-fold teacher is ~36.5 T4-hours and an all-data student ~16.7 T4-hours. AUDIT.md:258 measures ~10 TFLOPS achieved per T4. An H100 should give at least 12-25× per GPU on bf16 ViT-L without gradient checkpointing (assumption: well under its peak ratio). That puts the teacher at ~1.5-3 H100-hours (~$3-12) and a student at ~$1.5-6. Prices quoted Oct 2026: RunPod H100 PCIe $1.99 (community) / $2.89 (secure); A100 $1.19-1.59; L40S $0.79-1.09; 4090 $0.34-0.74; Lambda H100 SXM $3.99-4.29 and A100 SXM $2.79; Vast verified H100 ~$1.50-2.27. The host's ruling (REFERENCE.md:24-47) says sending Competition Data to an external service for computational processing is 'not, by itself, ... prohibited PRIVATE SHARING'. Use a datacenter or secure-cloud VM with a private encrypted disk, not peer-to-peer community hosts, and delete the data at the end.

ideas.title: Rent datacenter GPUs for all training; keep Kaggle GPU for inference and commit runs only
ideas.mechanism: Move train_windows.py runs (already a plain script with DDP, compile, bf16-capable autocast and fused SDPA) to a VM with 1-4 H100 or A100 80 GB GPUs. Pull the Stage B shards (62 GB) and Stage A (32 GB) with the kaggle CLI. Push weights back as a private Kaggle dataset. With 80 GB, drop gradient checkpointing, which removes ~25-33% recompute (AUDIT.md:260), and raise the micro-batch. The weekly loop becomes a same-day loop.
ideas.evidence_for: Measured cost: 0.105 s per window per T4 for Ortho Stage B 384, i.e. 36.5 T4-hours for the 4-fold teacher and 16.7 T4-hours for an all-data student. Achieved throughput is only ~10 TFLOPS per T4 (AUDIT.md:258). Inference is unaffected: weights are plain state dicts, and the existing core cell and parity fixture check sha, key sets and shapes. No rule restricts where training happens (see closed_too_early).

The teacher route's measured LB transfer is small (~0 to +0.005; (B) read −0.002, RUNBOOK.md:267-268), so compute amplifies a lever that may itself be weak. fastMRI-derived data must not go to cloud without reading its agreement (REFERENCE.md ~:133).

ideas.title: Use the quota-free scoring rerun as free compute: experiments trained inside the submission notebook
ideas.mechanism: The hidden rerun (up to 9 h on 2×T4) is not charged to quota (RUNBOOK.md:244). A builder mode that checks KAGGLE_IS_COMPETITION_RERUN would skip training in the commit run and, in the rerun, train a small or medium model on the attached Stage A/B caches before predicting the hidden test. At 5 a day that is up to ~45 free 2×T4 session-hours a day. The only readout is the leaderboard score; weights and OOF are not visible. It is therefore right for recipe A/B tests and wrong for teachers.
ideas.evidence_for: ResNet34 runs at 1.8-2.6 min/epoch on a T4 (fusion/runs_r34v2_B/bench.json), so 5 folds × 15 epochs on 2 T4s is ~1.5 h plus ~30 min of decode. A DDP CoAtNet fine-tune is ~7 × ~32 min ≈ 4 h plus inference, which fits under 9 h. Our own models' scoring is fast: the Ortho-alone read came back in 39 min and (B) in 79 (RUNBOOK.md:178-180). In-notebook training is a known pattern here (the prvsiyan lineage, docs/archive/IMPROVEMENTS.md §3c).
ideas.evidence_against: A 9-h timeout burns a daily slot. Seed noise (~0.002-0.003) adds to the ±0.005 paired leaderboard error. Nothing comes back to inspect, so the finals still need a normal retrain. It has not been checked that the competition train files and attached caches are mounted in the rerun (they normally are).
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Indirect, 0 to +0.010. It is the cheapest way to judge on image truth the CoAtNet-family label and recipe changes that the 691 cannot judge.
ideas.cost: 1 submission per experiment; ~0.5 day to build the rerun-aware mode; ~1-2 min of commit quota with the fast path.
ideas.fastest_test: A ResNet34 Stage A, 1 fold, 5 epochs, trained in the rerun. Check the quota page before and after: expect only the commit minutes charged. The score should land near the 691-calibrated value for that recipe (~0.88).

ideas.title: Treat the leaderboard as the main instrument on a budget, with per-finding probes
ideas.mechanism: ~97 submissions remain (2 today before 17:00 PDT, when they expire, plus 19 × 5). Allocate them roughly: ~12 per-finding probes, ~30 paired structural reads, ~20 in-rerun recipe reads, ~10 confirmations of final candidates, ~15 slack. Per-finding probe: submit a fast model's predictions for one finding with the other 11 columns at a constant 0.5, so that finding's public AUC = 12 × LB − 5.5. With 3-decimal rounding that is accurate to ±0.006, against a sampling error of ~0.02-0.03 at n≈400. Gold-58 per finding has SE 0.03-0.09. Decision rules: model vs model only if |Δ| ≥ 0.010; a blend change only if ≥ 0.004; never choose among more than 3 near-equal variants on the public set (the best of 4 at SE 0.005 is inflated by ~+0.005, the best of 10 by ~+0.008); keep a ledger of every submission.
ideas.evidence_for: The leaderboard is the only image-truth instrument (REFERENCE.md §1.4, §2). The rerun is quota-free. Our own models score in under 1.5 h, so 4-5 sequential reads a day are possible. No probing is used anywhere in the repo (grep finds no constant-column or probe code). The four weak findings (Synovitis, PF OA, Lateral OA, Lateral Meniscus at 0.81-0.87 on gold-58, RUNBOOK.md:189-193) need image-truth diagnosis that gold-58 cannot give.
ideas.evidence_against: The public 30% is not the private 70%. A probe must direct effort, never pick per finding (DECISIONS: per-finding picking is closed). Each stack read takes 8-9 h, so only ~2 stack reads a day are possible.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly. It concentrates compute and label work on the findings where the image graders actually differ, worth more than any one A/B if it finds a +0.05 finding (+0.004 macro each).
ideas.cost: ~12 submissions over 3-4 days, a few minutes of commit quota each.
ideas.time_to_first_signal: ~1 h per probe with the Ortho-alone notebook.
ideas.fastest_test: Today, with one expiring submission: the Ortho student r1 with only Synovitis live and 11 constant columns. Compare 12 × LB − 5.5 with its gold-58 Synovitis value (~0.82).

ideas.title: Use the 691 (GPT-5.6 reference) as the calibrated leaderboard proxy for the Ortho family
ideas.mechanism: LB ≈ 1.091 × 691 − 0.004 across four Ortho models (residuals ≤ 0.0014). Predict the leaderboard of every held-out Ortho run (and later CNN runs, once calibrated with two leaderboard points) from its 691 score within minutes. Spend a submission only to confirm a predicted structural jump or to judge what the 691 cannot see: CoAtNet started from the public init, and blends with the stack.
ideas.evidence_for: fusion/runs_*/score_runs_ortho.txt give 0.8298/0.8410/0.8440/0.8534 against LB 0.901/0.915/0.916/0.927. The fit holds across Stage A→B and steven_v2 → dread_soft → teacher targets.
ideas.evidence_against: Only 4 points, all from one family. Rule 3's concern (the reference is an LLM read of reports) could bite on a change that moves predictions toward image truth. All-data runs have no 691.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly. It saves ~1 submission per Ortho run and gives same-hour decisions.
ideas.cost: None; the scorer already exists (fusion/score_oof.py).
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Immediate for any run that keeps the 691 holdout.
ideas.fastest_test: Pre-register now: the next held-out Ortho run's leaderboard must fall within ±0.004 of 1.091 × 691 − 0.004. If it does, adopt the proxy for that family.

On the Mac it runs under launchd with caffeinate, on power. On cloud, use 4090s at $0.34-0.74/h, where a ResNet34 5-fold run is ~1 h, roughly $0.5. lens: THE ENDGAME: building the two final submissions that can win the PRIVATE leaderboard
headline: Swapping members inside the public stack cannot win from here. I fitted a one-parameter correlation model to our two blend reads (rho about 0.89). It says a family added at 1/3 must score about 0.943 alone to add +0.004, and a model replacing the core about 0.947, so (A) has roughly a 1-3% chance of reaching 0.947, and today's members cap the endgame near 0.945-0.949 (silver range); the private winner will sit near 0.957-0.960 true, because the public 0.961s carry about +0.003-0.005 of selection on 397 studies. The levers that remain are: runtime (decode is I/O-latency-bound and each of the stack's 7-10 input pipelines pays it again); two structurally different finals (stack-plus, and an untuned blend of the full public CoAtNet branch with an Ortho family whose public score is unbiased); and the hidden rerun, which does not use GPU quota, so submission slots are the cheap resource. Only a 0.95-class new member or a merger before 10-15 can realistically win.

what_went_wrong.title: A two-point linear 'exchange rate' led to a core swap that by construction could not differ from the core
what_went_wrong.evidence: The 0.2x rate (RUNBOOK.md:39-40) comes from Sub B 0.936 and Sub B-dread 0.939, each read to ±0.002. The same two points fit a probit/d' model with rho 0.885 and 0.904 (0.86-0.95 within noise). That model gives break-even at about 0.930 alone and a slope of about 0.27, not 0.936 and 0.2. The student was a 7-epoch, lr 3e-5 fine-tune of the converged CC0 core. Its train loss went 0.576 to 0.554 (fusion/runs_coatnet_student_r1_all/runs_coatnet/summary.json, hist) and its relative weight change was 0.0240 (RUNBOOK.md:177,184); (B) read -0.002 (RUNBOOK.md:260). Under the model, replacing the 29% core needs a core of about 0.947 alone for +0.004. P((A) >= 0.947) is about 1-3% (expected 0.942-0.943 ± 0.002), not the forecast's 1 in 4 (RUNBOOK.md:65).

ideas.title: Decompose the stack on the LB before any more swaps (chain alone, CoAt branch alone, minus calibrator, minus DINOv2)
ideas.mechanism:
Four inference-only submissions:
(a) Chain alone: public cells 0..-3, then publish `_pipeline_stage.csv`, which holds the chain's final ranks before cell -2 reads it.
(b) CoAt branch alone: cell -2's Raptor runner with all four raptor arms plus mattiaangeli's four at the published 0.6/0.4, an extension of --core-alone.
(c) The stack without its fitted calibrator.
(d) The stack without DINOv2.
With the stack's 0.943 and the core's 0.933 already read, fit rho per component, then price each option: add at 1/3, replace the chain, replace mattiaangeli-4, or Final 2.
ideas.evidence_for: The stage-file seam already exists and the builder checks it (build_submit_kernel.py:702, 740). --core-alone reuses cell -2's code verbatim and gave a clean paired read (0.933 vs 0.931). Each read costs about 6 GPU-min of commit run (RUNBOOK.md:244-246).
ideas.evidence_against: An alone score is ±0.008 and a component-vs-stack difference ±0.003-0.005. The per-finding overrides make a two-component model approximate. It uses 4 slots.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly. It decides between options worth +0.001 to +0.005 and prevents a wrong final.
ideas.cost: (a) 1-2 h of build; (b) 0.5-1 day; about 0.4 GPU-h of commit runs; 4 slots
ideas.time_to_first_signal: (a) can be submitted today before 17:00 PDT; its hidden run is only the chain's time
ideas.fastest_test: Chain-alone build: the --core-alone seam checks, cells 0..-3, a cell that copies `_pipeline_stage.csv` through the public publish cell; submit.

ideas.title: Time the stack per phase, then add a bit-exact I/O read-ahead warmer (and shared decode where possible)
ideas.mechanism: Parsing an uncompressed DICOM costs about 3.1 ms/slice, about 0.5 s for a ~159-file study. Kaggle measured 2.6-5.5 s/study/worker, so about 85% of decode is waiting on per-file I/O, and each of the stack's roughly 7-10 input pipelines re-reads about 210k hidden-test files. A background pool of 32-64 threads that reads the next N studies' files ahead of whichever branch is running (hooked on rsna_phase/rsna_deadline) turns that latency into page-cache hits; the outputs are identical by construction. If the timing shows decode dominating, the next step is study-major chunking: read each study once and run every branch on it.
ideas.evidence_for: FINDINGS.md:172-189; docs/archive/PLAN.md:295-310 ('the lever is concurrency of opens'); archive:958 and 229. My rough split: decode passes about 2.5-3.7 h (22 min each at 4 workers), CoAtNet forwards about 1.5 h (8 passes x 0.986 s/study/T4, runs_coatnet_student_r1_all summary.json), with the rest DINOv2/A5/Rad/loading.
ideas.evidence_against: The stack is the 'speedy raptors' and already prefetches windows (`_ke_prefetched_windows`). The real split is unmeasured, and the hidden-run mount may behave differently from a session's.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly. An estimated 1-3 h freed is room for 2-4 Ortho-class members or a third family (+0.001 to +0.004 each in a final).
ideas.cost: About 1 GPU-h for the stack on 100 train studies with the test root faked (x13 extrapolation), plus about 1 GPU-h with the warmer; 1-2 engineering days; a bit-exact parity check on 3 test + 20 train studies
ideas.time_to_first_signal: Today or tomorrow, from the ~4 h of quota left this week
ideas.fastest_test: Point find_test_root at a fake root holding 100 train studies; log the rsna_phase timestamps; rerun with the warmer; compare per-phase seconds per study.

ideas.title: Final 2 = the full public CoAt branch + an Ortho family at equal ranks, with nothing fitted (not Ortho + the student)
ideas.mechanism:
Rank-mean of two families:
- CoAt family: raptor v5/v5-rev/v8/v10 + mattiaangeli 4, mixed as cell -2 mixes them.
- Ortho family: mean of Ortho-all, r1 and any folds.
No chain, no calibrator, no per-finding overrides. Its public score is then an unbiased estimate of its private one, its errors differ from Final 1's, and its runtime is about 4-5 h.
ideas.evidence_for: The d' model: CoAt 0.943 + Ortho 0.937 gives 0.945-0.947 at rho 0.9-0.85, versus 0.939-0.941 with the student. The stack's +0.015 over its best single (RUNBOOK.md:36) comes from exactly this kind of family diversity. archive:181-190 makes the shake-up argument.
ideas.evidence_against: The CoAt branch's alone score is unread (it could be about 0.938), and Ortho-all is pending. Equal ranks may underweight a much stronger CoAt family. Rule 4: a weaker member costs.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Public -0.001 to +0.004 vs 0.943; private about +0.002 to +0.006 vs the stack's private
ideas.cost: About 1 day of build (idea 1(b) + the BLEND cell at w 0.5); about 10 GPU-min; 1-2 slots
ideas.fastest_test: Once 1(b) exists, rank-mean it 1:1 with Ortho-all and submit.

ideas.title: Verify off-quota hidden reruns, then turn submission slots into training compute
ideas.mechanism: The scoring rerun does not count against quota (RUNBOOK.md:244-246) and gets 9 h on 2 T4s with every attached input (the Stage A/B caches are kernel outputs). A submission that trains in the hidden run only, with a 1-step smoke in the commit run, then predicts, returns an LB read of a new model at zero quota. Examples: a CoAtNet from the public init with a real learning rate on new targets (7 epochs is about 3.8 h with DDP), a small CNN 5-fold (about 2 h), or a VLM epoch.
ideas.evidence_for: RUNBOOK.md:244. COMPETITION_RULES.txt only caps submissions per day and finals. A CoAtNet epoch is 63.8 min on one T4 (runs_coatnet_student_r1_all summary.json). Public and private scores come from the same run, so the read is the model.
ideas.evidence_against: Hidden-run outputs are invisible: no weights, no OOF, and a crash returns only 'error'. The quota claim must be verified. Winner obligations need reproducible training and published weights afterwards. Some may see it as against the spirit; check the forum and host rulings first.
ideas.expected_lb_gain: Indirect. It multiplies LB-judged single-model screens about 5-10x (labels, LR/epochs, recipes), the only way to search for a 0.945+ member in 19 days.
ideas.cost: 1 day for a train-then-infer wrapper (train_windows + infer_windows); 1 slot for the probe
ideas.fastest_test: Submit Ortho r1 alone (known 0.927) plus a 60-min GPU load in the hidden run only. Compare the weekly quota meter before and after.

ideas.title: One decode, many Ortho models: multi-weight infer_windows, with Ortho folds as members

Four more folds (about 5.7 GPU-h each at 8 epochs) double as round-2 OOF teachers and as a 5-fold member; fold-averaging is typically +0.003-0.006 alone.

ideas.title: Fail-loud experiment builds, plus a hidden-runtime probe
ideas.mechanism: Experiment builds raise in the hidden run on any raptor_neutral_fill, raptor_study_failed or deadline event, so a degraded run shows as 'error' and is never read as a model effect. Finals keep fill tolerance. Probe: set finding k to the constant 0.5 if and only if total elapsed > T0 + k x 10 min. The score then encodes the true hidden runtime to about ±10 min, at the cost of that submission's score.
ideas.evidence_for: build_submit_kernel.py:525-531 and :561; the stack's 8-h guard (archive:1044); a timed-out final scores nothing
ideas.evidence_against: An error burns a slot; the probe deliberately destroys its own score
ideas.expected_lb_gain: 0 directly; it protects every read and both finals
ideas.cost: 1-2 h; 1 slot for the probe
ideas.fastest_test: Add the hidden-run raise to the next experiment build.

winner_would: Q1, shake-up. Aim at about 0.957-0.960 true, not at the public #1. Going from about 397 public studies to about 925 private shrinks one score's SE from ±0.008 to ±0.0052, an independent-model difference from ±0.005 to ±0.0033, and a blend tweak to ±0.0013. Picking the best of k on the public LB inflates scores by SD x E[max]: for blend tweaks (SD 0.0014) +0.0022/0.0029/0.0035 at k=10/30/100; for model swaps (SD 0.0035) +0.005 to +0.009. So the three 0.961s are about 0.955-0.958 true, and the private winner lands near 0.957-0.960 on the public scale, plus an unknown common shift. The top 10 (spread 0.003) is a coin toss among themselves. The 0.943-0.947 band of stack forks shares the stack's own +0.002-0.003 tuning and will reshuffle by hundreds of places. Gold (top ~20 of 4,999) needs about 0.954-0.955 private; silver (top 250) about 0.945-0.947 by 10-22; we are at about 0.938-0.940 true.

Q2, runtime. Measure first: about 1 GPU-h on 100 train studies with rsna_phase timestamps, or the elapsed-time-encoding probe on the real hidden run. Then buy runtime where it is spent: an I/O read-ahead warmer (bit-exact) and, if decode-bound, study-major shared decode. Next, drop the chain in its slot-swap form. Only after that consider fp16 or fewer windows. Keep at least 45 min of measured margin in at least one final, and make every experiment fail loudly on fills or deadlines.

Q4, final selection. Write the rule before 10-16:
- Final 1 = the best stack-plus candidate, with at most 4 candidates; within 0.002, prefer fewer changed knobs.
- Final 2 = the best untuned family blend (no calibrator or overrides), at most 4 candidates.
- Ignore public gaps under 0.004 between structurally different candidates, and discount stack-shaped ones by about 0.002-0.003 for the tuning they inherit.
- Require measured hidden runtime with margin.
Two structurally different finals add about +0.001 to E[max] (0.4 x a private-difference SD of 0.0025), against about +0.0005 for two stack variants.

Q5, the blend that is realistic by 10-20 without a merger:
- Final 1 = the public CoAt branch as published (70%) + an Ortho family (Ortho-all + r1 + folds, one shared decode) in the chain's slot or at 1/3, with the warmer for runtime: about 0.946-0.949 public.
- Final 2 = equal-rank CoAt family + Ortho family, plus a third family only if it reads >= 0.930 alone: about 0.945-0.948 public, unbiased.
A winning blend needs three families each about 0.948-0.951 alone at pairwise residual rho <= 0.85 (gives about 0.957). Ours are about 0.933-0.945, so win-level upside comes only from a 0.95-class member (multi-source teacher labels, the VLM, or the small-CNN recipe gap) or from a merger.
